mishnayos.summary: In the month of Adar, beis din reminds everyone to bring their half-shekel and to pull out mixed plantings. In the middle of Adar they also fix roads and water pools, mark graves, and check the fields.

chunks.en: On the first of Adar, beis din announces about the shekalim,
chunks.st: On the first of Adar the court proclaims concerning the collection of shekels,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the yearly half-shekel contribution to the Temple treasury made by each adult male for the purpose of buying communal offerings.

words.note: The half-shekel coin every grown man gave each year to buy korbanos for everyone.

chunks.en: and about kilayim, mixed plantings.
chunks.st: And they also proclaim with regard to the obligation to uproot forbidden mixtures of diverse kinds of food crops in gardens and fields.

words.note: Planting different kinds of seeds together, which the Torah forbids.

chunks.he: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ קוֹרִין אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה בַּכְּרַכִּין,
chunks.en: On the fifteenth of Adar, the Megillah is read in the walled cities.
chunks.st: And on the fifteenth day of the month of Adar, the Scroll [Megilla] of Esther is read in the cities [kerakim] surrounded by walls from the time of Joshua.

words.note: Cities that had a wall around them from the time of Yehoshua.

chunks.en: And they fix the roads,
chunks.st: And they also repair the roads that were damaged in the winter,

chunks.en: the streets, and the water pools,
chunks.st: and the streets, and the cisterns.

chunks.en: and they do everything the public needs.
chunks.st: And at that time they perform all that is necessary for public welfare.

chunks.en: And they mark the graves,
chunks.explain: So people know where graves are and can stay tahor.
chunks.st: And they also mark the Jewish gravesites anew,
chunks.stMore: so that people would know their location and avoid ritual impurity, as the previous markers may have eroded during the rainy season.

chunks.en: and they also go out to check for kilayim.
chunks.st: And agents of the court also go out to inspect the fields for diverse kinds of food crops,
chunks.stMore: to determine whether or not the farmers had in fact uprooted these seeds after the proclamation on the first of the month. If the agents of the court found that these diverse kinds had not been uprooted, they themselves would uproot them.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehuda tells how beis din dealt with people who did not pull out their kilayim. In the end, they made the whole field ownerless.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: At first they would pull out the plants and throw them in front of the owners.
chunks.st: At first those agents would uproot the diverse kinds of crops and cast them in front of the owners of the fields.

chunks.en: When there were more people who did not listen,
chunks.st: When the number of transgressors who would not uproot diverse kinds in their fields increased, and the Sages saw that this tactic was ineffective,

chunks.en: they would pull them out and throw them onto the roads.
chunks.st: they would cast the uprooted crops onto the roads.

chunks.he: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַפְקִירִין כָּל הַשָּׂדֶה כֻּלָּהּ:
chunks.en: They made a rule that the whole field becomes hefker, free for anyone to take.
chunks.st: Ultimately, they instituted that the entire field should be declared ownerless.

mishnayos.stIntro: At the end of the last mishna it was stated that the court sends out agents on the fifteenth of Adar to inspect whether the owners of fields had indeed uprooted any diverse kinds of crops as instructed.

mishnayos.summary: In Adar, money changers sat at tables to collect the half-shekel, first around the country and later in the Beis HaMikdash. This mishnah teaches who had to give and who did not.

chunks.en: On the fifteenth of Adar,
chunks.st: On the fifteenth of Adar,

chunks.en: money changers sat at tables around the country.
chunks.st: money changers would sit at tables set up in the rest of the country, outside the Temple, to handle the collection of shekels.

words.note: Money changers who sat at tables to collect the half-shekel.

chunks.en: On the twenty-fifth, they sat in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: On the twenty-fifth of Adar, the money changers sat in the Temple.

chunks.en: Once they sat in the Beis HaMikdash, they began to take a pledge.
chunks.st: From the time when the money changers sat in the Temple, the court began to seize collateral from those who had yet to donate the half-shekel.

words.note: To take something of the person's until he paid his half-shekel.

chunks.en: From whom did they take a pledge?
chunks.st: From whom did they seize collateral?

chunks.en: From Levi'im, Yisraelim, geirim, and freed slaves,
chunks.st: From Levites, Israelites, converts, and emancipated slaves.

words.note: People who became Jewish.

chunks.en: but not from women, slaves, or children.
chunks.st: However, they did not seize collateral from women, slaves, or minors.

chunks.he: כָּל קָטָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל אָבִיו לִשְׁקוֹל עַל יָדוֹ,
chunks.en: Any child whose father began to give the half-shekel for him
chunks.st: And any minor whose father began one year to contribute a half-shekel on his behalf, despite the fact that he was not obligated to do so,

chunks.en: may not stop giving it.
chunks.st: he may not cease to do so in subsequent years.

chunks.en: They do not take a pledge from the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The court does not seize collateral from priests,
chunks.stMore: although they are legally obligated to give a half-shekel like all other Jews,

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: because of the ways of peace.
chunks.stMore: The mishna goes on to explain the status of priests with regard to the contribution of the half-shekel.

mishnayos.summary: Do Kohanim have to give the half-shekel? Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai says they must, and he explains the mistaken reason some Kohanim gave for not giving it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said

chunks.en: Ben Bukhri told this in Yavneh:
chunks.st: that ben Bukhri testified in Yavne:

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.
The town where the Sanhedrin sat after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed.

chunks.en: A Kohen who gives the half-shekel is not doing a sin.
chunks.st: Any priest who contributes the half-shekel is not considered a sinner, despite the fact that he is not obligated to do so.

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda added that Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said to ben Bukhri:

words.note: A great leader of the Jewish people.

chunks.en: "Not so!
chunks.st: Not so;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא כָּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹקֵל חוֹטֵא,
chunks.en: A Kohen who does not give it is doing a sin.
chunks.st: rather, any priest who does not contribute the half-shekel is considered a sinner, as they are obligated like all other Jews.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים דּוֹרְשִׁים מִקְרָא זֶה לְעַצְמָן,
chunks.en: But the Kohanim explain this pasuk in a way that helps themselves:
chunks.st: However, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai continued, the priests who do not contribute interpret this verse to their own advantage:

chunks.en: "Every mincha of a Kohen
chunks.st: “And every meal-offering of the priest

words.note: A korban made of flour.

chunks.en: must be burned completely; it may not be eaten."
chunks.st: shall be wholly made to smoke; it shall not be eaten” (Leviticus 6:16).

chunks.en: They say: since the omer and the two breads
chunks.st: Those priests claim as follows: Since the omer offering and the two loaves,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the public offering of two loaves from the new wheat brought on the festival of Shavuot,

words.note: A flour korban brought on the second day of Pesach.
Two loaves brought on Shavuos.

chunks.en: and the lechem hapanim would be ours too,
chunks.st: and the shewbread placed on the sacred table in the Sanctuary each Shabbat, which are all meal-offerings, are ours,
chunks.stMore: then if we contribute shekels we will have partial ownership of these communal offerings, as they are purchased with the shekels.

words.note: The lechem hapanim, the special loaves on the Shulchan in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: how could they be eaten?"
chunks.explain: They thought a Kohen's mincha may not be eaten, so they did not give.
chunks.st: How, then, can they be eaten?
chunks.stMore: They ought to be regarded as priests’ meal-offerings, which must be wholly burnt. But since these offerings are eaten, the priests concluded that they are not obligated to contribute the half-shekel. This argument does not, however, take into account the fact that communal offerings belong to the public, which is understood as its own entity, and are not regarded as shared offerings of all who contribute to the public purse.

mishnayos.summary: Women, slaves and children do not have to give the half-shekel, but if they give it, it is accepted. This mishnah also teaches which korbanos are taken from a non-Jew or a Kuti.

chunks.en: Even though they said
chunks.st: Although the Sages said, as stated in the previous mishna,

chunks.en: that they do not take a pledge from women, slaves, or children,
chunks.st: that the court does not seize collateral from women, slaves, and minors, as they are not obligated to contribute,

chunks.en: if they gave the half-shekel, it is taken from them.
chunks.st: however, if they contributed a shekel of their own accord, the Temple treasurers accept from them.

chunks.he: הַנָּכְרִי וְהַכּוּתִי שֶׁשָּׁקְלוּ, אֵין מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
chunks.en: If a non-Jew or a Kuti gave the half-shekel, it is not taken from them.
chunks.st: Conversely, in the case of a gentile or a Samaritan [Kuti] who contributed a shekel to participate in the communal offerings, they do not accept it from them.

words.note: The Kutim lived in Eretz Yisrael but were not counted as real Jews.

chunks.en: And they do not take from them the birds of a zav,
chunks.st: And likewise, they do not accept from a gentile or a Samaritan pairs of birds sacrificed in the purification ritual of a zav,

words.note: People who became tamei in a special way.

chunks.en: the birds of a zavah, or the birds of a woman who had a baby,
chunks.st: pairs of birds of a zava, or pairs of birds of a woman who gave birth, all of which are brought for ritual purification,

chunks.he: וְחַטָאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת. (אֲבָל) נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת, מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
chunks.en: or a chatas or an asham. But promised korbanos and gifts are taken from them.
chunks.st: or sin-offerings or guilt-offerings.

words.note: Korbanos brought for a sin.
Korbanos brought for certain sins.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Anything that can be promised or given as a gift is taken from them.
chunks.st: With regard to anything that can be brought to the altar as a vow or as a free-will offering, the priests accept it from gentiles and Samaritans,

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁאֵין נִדָּר וְנִדָּב אֵין מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
chunks.en: Anything that cannot be promised or given as a gift is not taken from them.
chunks.st: and with regard to anything that cannot be brought as a vow or as a free-will offering, they may not accept it from them.

chunks.he: וְכֵן הוּא מְפֹרָשׁ עַל יְדֵי עֶזְרָא,
chunks.en: And Ezra said this clearly,
chunks.st: And this principle was similarly articulated by Ezra,
chunks.stMore: when he recorded the Jewish leadership’s rejection of the Samaritans’ request to assist the Jews in the construction of the Second Temple,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "It is not for you and us
chunks.st: as it is stated: “But Zerubbabel, and Joshua, and the rest of the heads of fathers’ houses of Israel, said unto them: You have nothing to do with us

chunks.en: to build a house for our G-d."
chunks.st: to build a house unto our God;
chunks.stMore: but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord the God of Israel, as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us” (Ezra 4:3).

mishnayos.summary: Some people who give the half-shekel must also pay a small extra fee called a kalbon. This mishnah teaches who pays it and how many.

chunks.en: These are the people who must pay the kalbon:
chunks.st: And these are the people who are obligated in the premium [kalbon], a small sum added to the half-shekel collected:

words.note: A small extra fee added to the half-shekel.

chunks.en: Levi'im, Yisraelim, geirim, and freed slaves,
chunks.st: Levites, Israelites, converts, and emancipated Canaanite slaves,

chunks.he: אֲבָל לֹא כֹּהֲנִים וְנָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים.
chunks.en: but not Kohanim, women, slaves, or children.
chunks.st: but not priests, women, Canaanite slaves, or minors.

chunks.en: If someone gives the half-shekel for a Kohen,
chunks.st: One who contributes a half-shekel on behalf of a priest,

chunks.he: עַל יְדֵי אִשָּׁה, עַל יְדֵי עֶבֶד,
chunks.en: for a woman, or for a slave,
chunks.st: on behalf of a woman, on behalf of a slave,

chunks.en: or for a child, he does not have to pay a kalbon.
chunks.st: or on behalf of a child, is exempt from the premium, as they are exempt.

chunks.he: וְאִם שָׁקַל עַל יָדוֹ וְעַל יַד חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: But if he gave a whole shekel for himself and for his friend,
chunks.st: But if he contributed on his own behalf and on behalf of another,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he contributed one whole shekel to discharge both his own obligation and that of someone else,

chunks.en: he must pay one kalbon.
chunks.st: he is obligated in one premium.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says, two kalbons.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says: He must pay two premiums.

chunks.en: If someone gives a sela and takes back a half-shekel as change,
chunks.st: The mishna further states: One who gives the collection agent a sela, i.e., a whole shekel, and takes a shekel, i.e., a half-shekel, as change

words.note: A coin worth a whole shekel.
Here it means a half-shekel coin.

chunks.en: he must pay two kalbons.
chunks.st: is obligated in two premiums.

mishnayos.summary: If someone gives the half-shekel for a poor person or a neighbor, he does not pay the kalbon, but if he lends it, he does. The mishnah also says how much the kalbon is.

chunks.en: If someone gives the half-shekel for a poor person,
chunks.st: One who contributes a half-shekel on behalf of a poor person,

chunks.he: וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁכֵנוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי בֶּן עִירוֹ,
chunks.en: or for his neighbor, or for someone from his city,
chunks.st: on behalf of his neighbor, or on behalf of a resident of his city

chunks.en: he does not pay the kalbon.
chunks.st: is exempt from the premium.
chunks.stMore: The Sages did not obligate in the premium those who use their own money to fulfill the obligation of another.

chunks.en: But if he lent them the money, he must pay it.
chunks.st: But if one loaned them a half-shekel, rather than paying it on their behalf, he is obligated to pay the premium.
chunks.stMore: Since the recipients of the loan must repay the money, it is as though the half-shekel were paid from their property rather than the lender’s.

chunks.en: Brothers who are partners and must pay the kalbon
chunks.st: Partnered brothers, who have fully divided among themselves their late father’s assets, and who, if they jointly pay a whole shekel from those assets to discharge both of their obligations, are obligated in the premium like any other two private individuals,

chunks.en: do not have to give maaser from their animals.
chunks.st: are exempt from the animal tithe for the livestock they inherited.
chunks.stMore: Since they have completely divided between them all inherited assets, they are considered purchasers of the livestock, and a purchaser is exempt from the animal tithe.

words.note: Giving every tenth new animal as a korban.

chunks.en: And when they must give maaser from their animals,
chunks.st: But when they have not completely divided the assets, and they are therefore obligated in the animal tithe, as the livestock is considered in their father’s possession,

chunks.en: they do not pay the kalbon.
chunks.explain: It depends whether they already split up what their father left them.
chunks.st: they are exempt from the premium for their joint payment,
chunks.stMore: as in the case of one who pays on behalf of another.

chunks.en: And how much is a kalbon? A silver ma'ah,
chunks.st: And how much is a premium? A silver ma’a.

words.note: A small coin.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say, half a ma'ah.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: It is only half a ma’a.

mishnayos.summary: Towns far from Yerushalayim could change their shekalim into gold coins to carry them more easily. If the shekalim were stolen or lost on the way, this mishnah teaches who must swear and who must pay again.

chunks.en: They may change shekalim into big gold coins
chunks.st: they may combine their shekels and exchange them for darics [darkonot], which are large gold coins,

words.note: Large gold coins.

chunks.en: so they are not heavy to carry on the way.
chunks.st: due to the burden of the way.
chunks.stMore: Instead of carrying large amounts of shekels, the agents who deliver the funds will bring a much lighter burden of gold coins with them.

chunks.en: Just as there were collection boxes shaped like shofars in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: The mishna adds: Just as there were collection horns in the Temple to receive the half-shekel contributions,

words.note: Collection boxes shaped like a ram's horn.

chunks.en: so there were collection boxes around the country.
chunks.st: so too there were collection horns in the rest of the country,
chunks.stMore: i.e., areas outside of Jerusalem. The local inhabitants placed their half-shekels in these horns, which were later brought to Jerusalem.

chunks.en: If people of a town sent their shekalim
chunks.st: § With regard to the residents of a town who sent their shekels to the Temple

chunks.en: and they were stolen or lost on the way,
chunks.st: and they were stolen from the agent on the way or were lost,

chunks.en: if the terumah was already taken,
chunks.st: if the collection of the chamber had already been collected before these shekels arrived,

words.note: Taking money out of the shekalim room to buy korbanos.

chunks.en: the messengers swear to the treasurers of the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: the agents must take the oath of a bailee to the treasurers [gizbarin]. After the collection of the chamber,
chunks.stMore: all the shekels that have been contributed become the property of the Temple, so the Temple treasurers who are in charge of this property become the opposing litigants of the agents.

chunks.en: If not, they swear to the people of the town,
chunks.st: If the ceremony has not yet been performed and the contributions have not yet been collected into the baskets, the shekels are considered the property of the residents of the town, and therefore the agents must take an oath to absolve themselves to the residents of the town.
chunks.stMore: Since those shekels are still considered the property of the residents of the town because the shekels never reached the Temple, they have not fulfilled their obligation.

chunks.en: and the people of the town give other shekalim in their place.
chunks.st: Therefore, the residents of the town must contribute other shekels in their place.

chunks.en: If the lost shekalim were found, or the thieves gave them back,
chunks.st: If, after the residents of the town contributed other shekels, the original shekels were found or the thieves returned them,

chunks.en: both these and those are holy shekalim,
chunks.st: both these original shekels and those newly contributed ones have the status of consecrated shekels and belong to the Temple.

chunks.en: and they do not count for next year.
chunks.st: However, they do not count for the following year.
chunks.stMore: The people cannot claim that since they contributed twice in one year they are exempt from contributing the next year.

mishnayos.stIntro: When people who live far from Jerusalem wish to send to Jerusalem the shekels that have been levied from their community,

mishnayos.summary: If someone used his friend's half-shekel for himself, or gave his half-shekel from hekdesh money, he did me'ilah. If he gave it from maaser sheni or shemittah money, he must eat food worth the same amount in holiness.

chunks.he: הַנּוֹתֵן שִׁקְלוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ לִשְׁקֹל עַל יָדוֹ,
chunks.en: If someone gives his half-shekel to his friend to give for him,
chunks.st: With regard to one who gives his shekel to his fellow to contribute on his behalf by placing it in the collection horn for him,

chunks.en: and the friend gave it for himself,
chunks.st: and the fellow instead contributed it for himself,

chunks.en: if the terumah was already taken, he did me'ilah.
chunks.st: if at the time that he placed the shekel in the collection horn the collection of the chamber had been collected, the fellow is guilty of misuse of consecrated property.
chunks.stMore: When they perform the collection of the chamber, the treasurers also have in mind the shekels that have been contributed but are not yet in the possession of the Temple treasury, so that all those who have contributed shekels will have a part in the communal sacrifices. Therefore, when the agent gives this shekel for himself, he is considered to be deriving benefit from a consecrated item and is guilty of unintentional misuse of consecrated property.

words.note: Using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for yourself.

chunks.en: If someone gives his half-shekel from hekdesh money,
chunks.st: With regard to one who mistakenly contributes his shekel from consecrated money,

words.note: Things that belong to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: אִם נִתְרְמָה תְרוּמָה וְקָרְבָה הַבְּהֵמָה מָעַל.
chunks.en: once the terumah is taken and the animal is brought as a korban, he did me'ilah.
chunks.st: and then the collection of the chamber was collected and an animal purchased with those funds was sacrificed as a communal offering, he is guilty of misuse of consecrated property once the animal has been offered.
chunks.stMore: This is because at that point the money used to purchase the animal is transferred to non-sacred status. However, before that point, merely contributing consecrated money is not considered misuse.

chunks.en: If he gave it from maaser sheni money or shemittah money,
chunks.st: If one mistakenly contributed his shekel from money used to redeem the fruits of the second tithe or from money from the permitted sale of produce grown during the Sabbatical Year,

words.note: A tenth of the crops that was eaten in Yerushalayim.
The seventh year, when fields rest and the fruit is holy.

chunks.en: he must eat food worth the same amount, in holiness.
chunks.explain: Because he used holy money, he must replace it with his own.
chunks.st: he must eat non-sacred fruits besides the ones he already possesses, corresponding to the value of the shekel,
chunks.stMore: and he must treat them with the sanctity of second tithes or Sabbatical Year fruits.

mishnayos.summary: If someone gathered coins for his half-shekel and had extra left, is the extra holy? It depends on what he said when he gathered them.

chunks.he: הַמְכַנֵּס מָעוֹת וְאָמַר, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ לְשִׁקְלִי,
chunks.en: If someone gathers coins and says, "These are for my half-shekel,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who gathers together small coins and said: These are for my shekel,
chunks.stMore: and subsequently discovered that it amounted to more than a half-shekel.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say, the extra money goes for a gift korban.
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: The leftover coins are placed in the collection horn designated for a free-will offering,
chunks.stMore: as the money is consecrated property but it does not have the status of a shekel.

words.note: A korban given as a gift.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel say, the extra money is not holy.
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say: The leftover money is non-sacred property since,
chunks.stMore: ab initio, he had in mind to consecrate a half-shekel and no more. An item that was consecrated by mistake does not have the status of consecrated property.

chunks.en: If he said, "From these I will bring my half-shekel,"
chunks.st: However, if he originally said: I am gathering together this money so that I will bring my shekel from these,

chunks.en: they agree that the extra money is not holy.
chunks.st: they agree that the leftover money is non-sacred property.

chunks.en: If he said, "These are for my chatas,"
chunks.st: If one who was obligated to bring a sin-offering gathered together coins and said: These are for my sin-offering, then if he had accumulated more than was needed,

words.note: A korban brought for a sin.

chunks.en: they agree that the extra money goes for a gift korban.
chunks.st: they agree that the leftover money must be designated as a free-will offering.

chunks.en: If he said, "From these I will bring my chatas,"
chunks.st: However, if he originally said: That I will bring my sin-offering from these,

chunks.en: they agree that the extra money is not holy.
chunks.st: they agree that the leftover money is non-sacred property.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon explains why extra money for a half-shekel is not holy, but extra money for a chatas is. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon argue about whether the shekel has a set amount.

chunks.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַה בֵּין שְׁקָלִים לְחַטָאת.
chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said, What is the difference between shekalim and a chatas?
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the difference between shekels and a sin-offering?
chunks.stMore: Why do Beit Hillel say that the leftover money is non-sacred property in the case of shekels, while with regard to a sin-offering they say that the leftover money is consecrated for a free-will offering?

chunks.en: Shekalim have a set amount,
chunks.st: Rather, the issue is that shekels have a fixed value,
chunks.stMore: a half-shekel and no more. Therefore, there is a clear amount beyond which one did not intend the money to become consecrated property.

chunks.en: but a chatas has no set amount.
chunks.st: However, a sin-offering has no fixed value.
chunks.stMore: Since the entire sum that one collected could have been used to purchase a sin-offering, whatever he didn’t use must at least be designated for a free-will offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Even shekalim have no set amount.
chunks.st: Even for shekels there is no real fixed value.

chunks.en: For when the Jewish people came up from galus,
chunks.st: For when the Jewish people ascended from the exile,

words.note: Living outside Eretz Yisrael, away from the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: they gave darkonos as shekalim.
chunks.st: they would contribute darics,
chunks.stMore: which are Median coins worth two shekels by Torah law. They brought these coins with them and would give a half of one to fulfill their half-shekel obligation.

words.note: Large gold coins.

chunks.en: Then they went back to giving sela'im,
chunks.st: Later on, when the Median Empire was dissolved, they reverted to contributing with a sela,
chunks.stMore: a silver coin of equal weight to the the shekel mentioned in the Torah. People would contribute a half-sela for their half-shekel requirement.

words.note: Silver coins, each worth a whole shekel.

chunks.en: then they went back to giving tiv'in,
chunks.st: When the value of this currency changed later on, they reverted to contributing with a tiva, a different coin which is worth a half-shekel.

words.note: Coins worth half a shekel.

chunks.en: and they wanted to give dinarim.
chunks.st: Some people wished to contribute only dinars, which are half the value of the tiva, i.e., one quarter shekel in value. The Sages refused to accept it
chunks.stMore: and required them to contribute at least the half-shekel mentioned in the Torah. Nevertheless, it is clear that the obligation of contributing shekels does not have a fixed value.

words.note: Coins worth a quarter of a shekel.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said in response:

chunks.en: "Even so,
chunks.st: Even so,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that during different periods there were different amounts used to fulfill the obligation of the half-shekel,

chunks.en: everyone gives the same amount.
chunks.st: everyone has equal standing,
chunks.stMore: i.e., at any particular time, everyone contributes the same amount. Therefore, any sum collected beyond that amount was not intended to be consecrated.

chunks.en: But a chatas,
chunks.st: However, a sin-offering has no fixed amount whatsoever;

chunks.en: this person brings one worth a sela,
chunks.st: this person may bring an animal worth a sela,

chunks.en: and this one brings one worth two,
chunks.st: and that one may bring one worth two,

chunks.en: and this one brings one worth three."
chunks.st: and this one may bring one worth three. Therefore,
chunks.stMore: it cannot be supposed that there was no intention to consecrate the whole sum.

mishnayos.summary: What happens to money left over after buying a korban or after collecting for the poor, captives or the dead? Each kind of leftover money goes to a fitting place.

chunks.en: Leftover shekalim money is not holy.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what was set aside for shekels is non-sacred property,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with the opinion of Beit Hillel in the previous mishna. The mishna now discusses similar cases for other sacred items:

chunks.en: Leftover money from the tenth of an eifah of flour,
chunks.st: However, with regard to the leftover money from what one set aside to purchase the tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering

words.note: A measure of flour.

chunks.en: leftover money from the birds of zavim, the birds of zavos,
chunks.st: and the leftover money from what one set aside to purchase offerings that he is liable to sacrifice due to ritual impurity or a sin, such as the pairs of birds of a zav, the pairs of birds of a zava,

chunks.en: the birds of women who had a baby, and chataos and ashamos,
chunks.st: and the pairs of birds of a woman after childbirth, sin-offerings, or guilt-offerings,

chunks.en: their extra money goes for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: in these cases, its leftover money must be used for free-will offerings
chunks.stMore: that are offered as repletion of the altar, i.e., burnt-offerings sacrificed at times when the altar was idle.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁהוּא בָּא לְשֵׁם חַטָאת וּלְשֵׁם אַשְׁמָה,
chunks.en: Any money that comes for a chatas or for an asham,
chunks.st: Whatever money is designated for a sin-offering or for a guilt-offering,

chunks.en: its extra money goes for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: its leftover money must be used for a free-will offering.

chunks.en: Extra money for an olah goes for an olah.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase a burnt-offering that he owes, due to a vow or to volunteering, must be used for another burnt-offering that he will bring in the future.

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: Extra money for a mincha goes for a mincha.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase fine flour for a meal-offering must be used for another meal-offering.

chunks.en: Extra money for shelamim goes for shelamim.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase a peace-offering must be used for another peace-offering.

words.note: A korban that is shared by the mizbeach, the Kohanim and the owner.

chunks.en: Extra money for the korban Pesach goes for shelamim.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase a lamb for his Paschal lamb is not used for another Paschal lamb, such as for the following year. Rather, it is used for purchasing a peace-offering.

chunks.en: Extra money for nezirim goes for nezirim.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase sacrifices for a number of nazirites must be used to purchase sacrifices for other nazirites.

words.note: People who promised not to drink wine or cut their hair for a time.

chunks.en: Extra money for one nazir goes for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: The leftover money from what a single nazirite set aside for his own offering must be used for a free-will offering.

chunks.en: Extra money for the poor goes to the poor.
chunks.st: The leftover money collected for freeing unspecified captives must be allocated to freeing captives. The leftover money collected for freeing a specific captive is given as a gift to that captive. The leftover money collected as charity for the poor must be allocated to the poor.

chunks.he: מוֹתַר עָנִי, לְאוֹתוֹ עָנִי. מוֹתַר שְׁבוּיִים, לַשְּׁבוּיִים.
chunks.en: Extra money for one poor person goes to that poor person. Extra money for captives goes to captives.
chunks.st: The leftover money collected for a specific poor person is given as a gift to that poor person.

words.note: People taken prisoner who need to be freed.

chunks.he: מוֹתַר שָׁבוּי, לְאוֹתוֹ שָׁבוּי. מוֹתַר הַמֵּתִים, לַמֵּתִים.
chunks.en: Extra money for one captive goes to that captive. Extra money for the dead goes for the dead.
chunks.explain: Money collected to bury people is used to bury others.
chunks.st: The leftover money collected for burying the dead must be allocated to burying the dead.

chunks.en: Extra money for one dead person goes to his family.
chunks.st: The leftover money collected to bury or provide burial shrouds for a particular deceased person is given to his heirs.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says: It is uncertain what should be done,

chunks.he: מוֹתַר הַמֵּת, יְהֵא מֻנָּח עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: extra money for one dead person should be put away until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.explain: Eliyahu HaNavi will come and teach us what to do with it.
chunks.st: and therefore the leftover money for the deceased should be placed in a safe place until Elijah comes and teaches what should be done.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nosson says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Natan says:

chunks.he: מוֹתַר הַמֵּת בּוֹנִין לוֹ נֶפֶשׁ עַל קִבְרוֹ:
chunks.en: with extra money for a dead person they build a monument on his grave.
chunks.st: With the leftover money collected for a deceased person they build a monument [nefesh] on his grave for him.

mishnayos.summary: Three times a year, money was taken out of the shekalim room to buy korbanos. Rabbi Akiva says these are also the times for maaser of animals, and other Rabbis give different dates.

chunks.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה פְּרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה, תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַלִּשְׁכָּה,
chunks.en: Three times a year they take money out of the lishkah:
chunks.st: On three occasions during the year the ceremony of the collection of the Temple treasury chamber is performed. During the ceremony,
chunks.stMore: a priest enters the treasury chamber with three containers, lifts up [torem] some of the coins, and places them in the containers. These funds, known as the collection of the chamber, are used to purchase animals for communal offerings and other needs of the Temple.

words.note: The room in the Beis HaMikdash where the shekalim were kept.

chunks.en: half a month before Pesach,
chunks.st: These three occasions are: Half a month, fifteen days, before Passover, on the day before the first of the month of Nisan;

chunks.en: half a month before Shavuos,
chunks.st: half a month before Shavuot, on or around the twentieth of Iyar;

words.note: Another name for Shavuos.

chunks.en: and half a month before Sukkos.
chunks.st: half a month before the festival of Sukkot, on the day before Rosh HaShana.

words.note: Sukkos.

chunks.en: These are also the set times for maaser of animals.
chunks.st: These three days are also the due dates that were established by the Sages for the setting aside of animal tithes.
chunks.stMore: On each of these days one is obligated to tithe the animals that were born during the intervening period, and it is prohibited for him to eat or sell them until he does so.

words.note: Giving every tenth new animal as a korban.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says,
chunks.st: Ben Azzai says
chunks.stMore: that the dates established by the Sages for the setting aside of animal tithes are

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: on the twenty-ninth of Adar,
chunks.st: the twenty-ninth of Adar,

chunks.en: on the first of Sivan, and on the twenty-ninth of Av.
chunks.st: the first of Sivan, and the twenty-ninth of Av.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say that the dates for the animal tithes are

chunks.en: on the first of Nisan, on the first of Sivan,
chunks.st: the first of Nisan, the first of Sivan,

chunks.en: and on the twenty-ninth of Elul.
chunks.st: and the twenty-ninth of Elul.

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל,
chunks.en: Why did they say the twenty-ninth of Elul
chunks.st: And why did Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say the twenty-ninth of Elul

chunks.en: and not the first of Tishrei?
chunks.st: and not the first of Tishrei, as they said the first of Nisan and Sivan?

chunks.en: Because it is Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: The first of Tishrei is Rosh Hashanah.
chunks.st: Because the first of Tishrei is the festival of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: and we may not give maaser on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: and it is not permitted to tithe on a Festival.

chunks.en: So they made it earlier, on the twenty-ninth of Elul.
chunks.st: Therefore, the Sages advanced the day of tithing the animals born over the course of the summer to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

mishnayos.summary: The money was taken out with three baskets marked with letters. The one taking it wore clothes with no place to hide coins, so no one would suspect him of stealing.

chunks.en: With three baskets
chunks.st: The funds are collected from the Temple treasury chamber with three baskets,

chunks.en: each holding three se'ah, they take money out of the lishkah.
chunks.st: each measuring three se’a.

words.note: A measure for how much a basket holds.

chunks.en: And on them is written Alef, Beis, Gimmel.
chunks.st: On the baskets is written, respectively, alef, beit, gimmel,
chunks.stMore: based on the order in which the baskets are filled, to indicate from which basket coins should be taken to buy sacrifices. The coins were used in the order of their collection.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.he: יְוָנִית כָּתוּב בָּהֶן אָלפ"א בֵית"א גָמל"א.
chunks.en: In Greek is written on them Alfa, Beta, Gamma.
chunks.st: The letters written on them were in Greek, alfa, beta, gamma.

chunks.he: אֵין הַתּוֹרֵם נִכְנָס לֹא בְּפַרְגּוֹד חָפוּת,
chunks.en: The one taking out the money may not go in wearing a garment with folds,
chunks.explain: Folds where coins could be hidden.
chunks.st: The one who collects the funds from the chamber must not enter while wearing a cuffed garment [ḥafut],

chunks.en: and not with a shoe, and not with a sandal,
chunks.st: and not with a shoe, and not with a sandal,

chunks.en: and not with tefillin, and not with a kamei'a.
chunks.explain: All these have places where a coin could be hidden.
chunks.st: and not with phylacteries, and not with an amulet,
chunks.stMore: since all of these have places into which money can be inserted.

words.note: A small charm people wore for protection.

chunks.en: Maybe he will become poor,
chunks.st: The concern is that perhaps the one collecting the funds will one day become poor,

chunks.en: and people will say he became poor because of a sin with the lishkah money.
chunks.st: and people will say that it is because of the sin of stealing the shekels of the chamber that he became poor,
chunks.stMore: as they will suspect that he stole money and hid it in those places.

chunks.en: Or maybe he will become rich,
chunks.st: Or perhaps he will become rich

chunks.en: and people will say he became rich from the lishkah money.
chunks.st: and people will say that he became rich from stealing the funds of the chamber, even though he did not actually do so.
chunks.stMore: Even though one should not suspect someone of stealing consecrated shekels, the one collecting the funds from the chamber must nevertheless take these precautions,

chunks.he: לְפִי שֶׁאָדָם צָרִיךְ לָצֵאת יְדֵי הַבְּרִיּוֹת
chunks.en: Because a person must make sure people see he is innocent,
chunks.st: as a person must appear justified before people

chunks.en: just as he must be innocent before Hashem,
chunks.st: just as he must appear justified before the Omnipresent [HaMakom],

chunks.he: שְׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר לב) וִהְיִיתֶם נְקִיִים מֵיְיָ וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "You shall be clean before Hashem and before Yisrael."
chunks.st: and it is stated: “And you shall be guiltless before the Lord and before Israel”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 32:22). From here it may be inferred that it is not enough to be innocent before God; one must also be innocent before the Jewish people. Even in situations where there is little concern that one may commit a sin, the proper course is to remain above any possible suspicion of misconduct.

chunks.en: And it says, "And find favor
chunks.st: And the verse states: “So shall you find grace

chunks.en: and good sense in the eyes of G-d and people."
chunks.st: and good understanding in the sight of God and man” (Proverbs 3:4).

mishnayos.summary: Members of Rabban Gamliel's family wanted their own half-shekel to be used for the korbanos, so they tossed it right in front of the one taking out the money. Before he took the money, he asked permission three times.

chunks.en: Someone from the family of Rabban Gamliel
chunks.st: of the house of Rabban Gamliel
chunks.stMore: desired that their shekels be the ones collected from the chamber and used for the purchase of the communal offerings.

chunks.en: would come in with his half-shekel between his fingers,
chunks.st: Each of them would therefore come to the Temple specifically on the day of the ceremony of the collection of the chamber, enter the chamber with his shekel between his fingers,

chunks.en: and throw it in front of the one taking out the money.
chunks.st: and toss it in front of the one collecting
chunks.stMore: the money so that he would see it and place it in the basket containing the money to be taken out of the chamber.

chunks.en: And the one taking out the money would mean to push it into the basket.
chunks.st: Understanding what was happening, the one collecting the money from the chamber would purposely push this shekel into the basket, so that it would later be used to buy communal offerings.

chunks.he: אֵין הַתּוֹרֵם תּוֹרֵם עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהֶם,
chunks.en: The one taking out the money does not take it until he says to them,
chunks.st: The one collecting the funds from the chamber may not begin to collect the money until he asks the Temple treasurers three times:

chunks.en: "Shall I take?" And they say to him,
chunks.st: Shall I collect the funds, and they say to him:

chunks.en: "Take, take, take," three times.
chunks.st: Collect them, collect them, collect them, three times.

mishnayos.stIntro: In order to indicate the importance that was attached to the ceremony of the collection of the Temple treasury chamber, the mishna relates that the members

mishnayos.summary: After taking money from each big basket, the one taking it covered the basket so he would not take from it again. Each basket was taken for the sake of Jews in a different place.

chunks.en: He took money from the first basket and covered it with leather covers.
chunks.st: After he collected the funds from the first large basket and put them into one of the smaller baskets labeled with the letter alef, he immediately covered with a leather cover the large basket from which he had removed the money.

chunks.en: From the second, and covered it with leather covers.
chunks.st: After collecting funds from the second large basket, he covered it with a leather cover as well.

chunks.en: The third he did not cover.
chunks.st: But after collecting funds from the third large basket, he did not cover it.

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁכַּח וְיִתְרֹם מִן הַדָּבָר הַתָּרוּם.
chunks.en: He covered them in case he forgets and takes again from a basket he already took from.
chunks.st: The mishna asks: Why did he cover the first two baskets? In order to mark them as already having had funds collected from them. In this way, there was no concern that perhaps he would forget and once again collect funds from a basket from which funds had already been collected.

chunks.he: תָּרַם אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה לְשֵׁם אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: He took from the first one for the sake of Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: The mishna specifies the intent of the one collecting the funds from the baskets as he does so: He collected funds from the first basket on behalf of the people living in Eretz Yisrael;

chunks.en: the second one for the walled cities near it,
chunks.st: from the second basket on behalf of the people living in the cities near Eretz Yisrael;

chunks.en: and the third one for the sake of Bavel,
chunks.st: and from the third basket on behalf of the people living in Babylonia,

chunks.en: and for the sake of Madai,
chunks.st: and on behalf of the people living in Media,

words.note: A far country, Media.

chunks.en: and for the sake of faraway countries.
chunks.st: and on behalf of the people living in the distant countries.

mishnayos.stIntro: The coins were stored in the Temple treasury in three large baskets, each measuring nine se’a. In the collection of the chamber ceremony, coins were removed from these baskets and placed in smaller baskets of three se’a each that were marked with letters (see the previous mishna on daf 8a).

mishnayos.summary: The money taken out of the shekalim room was used to buy the korbanos of all the Jewish people. It also paid the guards who watched the grain for the omer in the shemittah year.

chunks.en: What did they do with the money that was taken out?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: The collection of half-shekels, what would they do with it?

chunks.en: They bought with it the daily korbanos,
chunks.st: They would purchase animals for the daily offerings, which were offered each morning and afternoon;

words.note: The korbanos brought every morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: the musaf korbanos and their wine offerings,
chunks.st: and for the additional offerings, which were offered on Shabbat, the New Moon, and Festivals; and wine for their libations;

words.note: Extra korbanos for Shabbos, Rosh Chodesh and Yom Tov.

chunks.en: the omer, the two breads, and the lechem hapanim,
chunks.st: barley for the omer meal-offering; and wheat for both the two loaves offered on Shavuot and the shewbread;

chunks.en: and all the korbanos of the whole community.
chunks.st: and animals for all the communal offerings.

chunks.en: The guards of the grain that grew by itself in the shemittah year
chunks.st: § The guards of the sefiḥin, grain that grew without being purposely planted, during the Sabbatical Year,
chunks.stMore: ensured that people did not take this ownerless grain, so that it remained available to be used for the omer and the offering of the two loaves.

chunks.en: get paid from the lishkah money.
chunks.st: They collect their wages from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: "Whoever wants may even offer to guard for free."
chunks.st: One who so desires may even volunteer his services and guard the grain as an unpaid bailee.

chunks.en: They said to him, "Even you say
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him: Even you must say that the omer and the two loaves

chunks.en: that these come only from the money of the whole community."
chunks.explain: If a person guards it for free, it becomes partly his.
chunks.st: come only from communal funds and not from any one individual.
chunks.stMore: If one were to volunteer his services, he would acquire the grain for himself by guarding it and transporting it to the Temple. In that case, these offerings would have come from an individual. So that the offerings come solely from communal funds, the guards must receive payment from the half-shekels removed from the chamber.

mishnayos.stIntro: At certain times of the year, half-shekels that had been donated to the Temple and stored in a chamber in the Temple were collected in order to be used for various purposes.

mishnayos.summary: The money from the lishkah also paid for the parah adumah, the se'ir hamishtalei'ach, and the red wool. The leftover money paid for ramps, the water channel, and the walls and needs of Yerushalayim.

chunks.he: פָּרָה וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ וְלָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית,
chunks.en: The parah adumah, the se'ir hamishtalei'ach, and the red wool strip
chunks.st: The red heifer, the scapegoat, and the strip of crimson wool used in the process of burning the red heifer all

words.note: The red cow whose ashes make people tahor.
The goat sent away on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: come from the lishkah money.
chunks.st: come from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber, despite the fact that they are not sacrificial offerings.

chunks.en: The ramp for the parah adumah,
chunks.st: The same is true for the ramp built from the Temple Mount to the location on the Mount of Olives, where they would slaughter the red heifer;

chunks.en: and the ramp for the goat that is sent away,
chunks.st: the ramp built to lead the scapegoat out of the city;

chunks.en: and the red strip between its horns,
chunks.st: the strip of crimson wool that was tied between its horns;

chunks.en: and the water channel,
chunks.st: any repairs required for the aqueduct that ran through the Temple courtyard

chunks.en: and the wall of the city and its towers,
chunks.st: and the walls of the city and its towers;

chunks.en: and everything the city needs,
chunks.st: and for all the needs of the city, such as street repairs, security, and the like.

chunks.en: come from the leftover money in the lishkah.
chunks.st: All of these come from the remains of the chamber,
chunks.stMore: i.e., from the money that remained in the chamber after the three collections of money were taken to use for communal offerings.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says,
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: The ramp for the parah, the Kohanim Gedolim
chunks.st: The High Priests construct the ramp for the red heifer

words.note: The Kohen Gadol is the head Kohen.

chunks.en: build it with their own money.
chunks.st: from their own funds.

mishnayos.summary: What was done with the money left over in the lishkah? Rabbi Yishmael says they bought wine, oil and flour to sell, and Rabbi Akiva says we do not make a profit with hekdesh money.

chunks.he: מוֹתַר שְׁיָרֵי הַלִּשְׁכָּה מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן,
chunks.en: What did they do with the extra money left in the lishkah?
chunks.st: What would they do with the leftover remains of the chamber after all the items mentioned above had been attended to?

chunks.en: They bought wines, oils, and fine flour with it,
chunks.explain: They sold these to people who needed them for their korbanos.
chunks.st: They would purchase wine, oil, and fine flour
chunks.stMore: and sell them to those who needed them for their private offerings.

chunks.en: and the profit goes to hekdesh.
chunks.st: And the profit from these sales would go to consecrated property, i.e., to the Temple treasury; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yishmael says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: We do not make a profit with hekdesh money,
chunks.st: One may not generate profit by selling consecrated property,

chunks.en: and not with money for the poor.
chunks.st: neither may one profit from funds set aside for the poor.

mishnayos.summary: What was done with extra money from the terumah? It covered the walls of the Kodesh HaKodashim with gold. The Rabbis argue about what to do with other leftover things.

chunks.he: מוֹתַר תְּרוּמָה מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ,
chunks.en: What did they do with the extra terumah money?
chunks.st: What would they do with the leftover funds of the collection that had not been spent on communal offerings?

chunks.he: רִקּוּעֵי זָהָב צִפּוּי לְבֵית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
chunks.en: Thin gold sheets to cover the Kodesh HaKodashim.
chunks.st: They would purchase golden plates as a coating for the walls and floor of the Holy of Holies.

words.note: The Kodesh HaKodashim, the holiest room in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: Extra fruit goes for extra olah korbanos on the mizbeach,
chunks.st: The leftover produce was used to purchase the repletion of the altar,
chunks.stMore: i.e., burnt-offerings sacrificed at times when the altar was idle.

words.note: Olah korbanos brought when the mizbeach had nothing else on it.

chunks.en: and extra terumah money goes for the vessels of the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: The leftover funds of the collection were used to purchase sacred vessels.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: Extra terumah money goes for extra olah korbanos on the mizbeach,
chunks.st: The leftover funds of the collection were used to purchase the animals used for the repletion of the altar, since they had originally been collected for offerings.

chunks.en: and extra wine offering money goes for the vessels.
chunks.st: The leftover libations were used to purchase sacred vessels.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chananya, the assistant Kohen Gadol, says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥananya, the deputy [segan] High Priest, says:

chunks.en: Extra wine offering money goes for extra olah korbanos,
chunks.st: The leftover libations were used to purchase animals for the repletion of the altar,

chunks.en: and extra terumah money goes for the vessels.
chunks.st: while the leftover funds of the collection were used to purchase sacred vessels.

chunks.he: זֶה וָזֶה לֹא הָיוּ מוֹדִים בַּפֵּרוֹת:
chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Chananya did not agree with Rabbi Yishmael about the fruit.
chunks.st: Both this Sage, Rabbi Akiva, and that Sage, Rabbi Ḥananya, did not agree with Rabbi Yishmael’s opinion with regard to the leftover produce.

mishnayos.summary: Ketores left over from last year could not be used with new money. So they paid the workers with it and then bought it back with the new shekalim.

chunks.he: מוֹתַר הַקְּטֹרֶת מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ,
chunks.en: What did they do with the extra ketores?
chunks.explain: It was bought with last year's money, and every year needs new money.
chunks.st: The leftover incense from one year could not be used the following year, as it had been purchased with the shekels collected for the previous year. What would be done with it in order to make it usable?

words.note: The special spices burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: They set aside from it the amount of the workers' pay,
chunks.st: The Temple treasurers would set aside an amount of it equal to the value of the wages of the artisans who worked in the Temple.

chunks.en: and they move its holiness onto the money owed to the workers,
chunks.st: They would then desacralize that incense by transferring its sanctity to the money owed to the artisans.

words.en: and they make it not holy

chunks.en: and they give it to the workers as their pay.
chunks.st: They would then give the incense to the artisans as their wages.

chunks.en: Then they buy it back with the new terumah money.
chunks.st: Finally, they would return and buy back the incense from the artisans with funds from the new collection of shekels.

chunks.en: If the new money came on time,
chunks.st: If the new funds come on time, i.e., by the beginning of Nisan,

chunks.en: they buy it with the new terumah money.
chunks.st: they purchase the incense with funds from the new collection of shekels.

chunks.en: And if not, with the old money.
chunks.st: And if not, they may still purchase it from the old collection, and it is valid.

mishnayos.summary: If someone gave all his things to hekdesh and some could be used for korbanos, how are they made into korbanos? Rabbi Akiva and Ben Azzai explain how it is done through the workers' pay.

chunks.en: If someone makes all his things hekdesh,
chunks.st: One who consecrates all his possessions without specifying for what purpose,
chunks.stMore: his possessions are consecrated for Temple maintenance.

chunks.he: וְהָיוּ בָּהֶן דְּבָרִים רְאוּיִין לְקָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר,
chunks.en: and among them are things fit for the korbanos of the community,
chunks.st: And if among them there are items that are suitable for use as communal offerings,
chunks.stMore: which may not be used for the maintenance of the Temple but only for sacrificial purposes, what is done with those items to remove their consecration for Temple maintenance, in order that they may be reconsecrated for sacrificial use?

chunks.en: they are given to the workers as their pay.
chunks.explain: The workers who fixed up the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: They are given to Temple artisans as their wages, and thereby they are desacralized; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai said to him,
chunks.st: Ben Azzai said to him:

chunks.en: "That is not the way.
chunks.st: This is not the method to be used.

chunks.en: Rather, they set aside from them the amount of the workers' pay,
chunks.st: Rather, the same method that is used to desacralize the leftover incense, as is described in the previous mishna, should also be used here, i.e., they set aside from the consecrated items the equivalent of the value owed to the artisans for their wages,

chunks.en: and move their holiness onto the workers' money,
chunks.st: and they desacralize them by transferring their sanctity onto the money allocated for the artisans’ wages,

words.en: and they make them not holy

chunks.en: and give them to the workers as their pay,
chunks.st: and then they give those items, which are no longer consecrated, to the artisans as their wages.

chunks.en: and then buy them back with the new terumah money."
chunks.st: According to both opinions, once the desacralized items are in the possession of the artisans, one of Temple treasurers should repurchase those items using money from that year’s new collection of half-shekels,
chunks.stMore: consecrating them for sacrificial use during the coming year.

mishnayos.summary: If someone gave all his things to hekdesh, including animals that could be korbanos, what happens to the animals? Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue, and Rabbi Papias says each one is right in a different case.

chunks.en: If someone makes all his things hekdesh,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates all his possessions without specifying for what purpose,

chunks.he: וְהָיְתָה בָּהֶן בְּהֵמָה רְאוּיָה לְגַבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: and among them is an animal fit for the mizbeach,
chunks.st: and among them there is an animal that is suitable to be sacrificed on the altar,

chunks.en: males and females,
chunks.st: male or female, what should be done with it?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: Since he did not specify otherwise,
chunks.stMore: everything is consecrated for Temple maintenance.

chunks.en: the males are sold to be olah korbanos,
chunks.st: Therefore, any males should be sold for the needs of burnt-offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such.

chunks.en: and the females are sold to be shelamim korbanos,
chunks.st: And any females, since they cannot be brought as burnt-offerings, should be sold for the needs of peace-offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such.

chunks.he: וּדְמֵיהֶן יִפְּלוּ עִם שְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבָּיִת.
chunks.en: and their money goes with the rest of his things to fix the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: And their monetary value that is received from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
chunks.stMore: Although he did not specify for what purpose he consecrated his possessions, it may be assumed that he intended the animals to be consecrated as burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: the males themselves are brought as olah korbanos,
chunks.st: Therefore, any males should themselves be sacrificed as burnt-offerings,

chunks.en: and the females are sold to be shelamim korbanos,
chunks.st: and any females, since they cannot be brought as burnt-offerings, should be sold for the needs of peace-offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such,

chunks.en: and with their money he brings olah korbanos,
chunks.st: and their monetary value that is received from their sale should be used to purchase and bring burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: and the rest of his things go to fix the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: According to both opinions, the rest of the possessions, which are not suitable for sacrificial use, are allocated for Temple maintenance.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.he: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
chunks.en: I see the words of Rabbi Eliezer as better
chunks.st: I see the statement of Rabbi Eliezer as more correct

chunks.en: than the words of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: than the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua,

chunks.en: because Rabbi Eliezer made his rule the same for everything,
chunks.st: since Rabbi Eliezer applied his method equally
chunks.stMore: to both animals and other possessions in treating both as consecrated for Temple maintenance,

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehoshua split them.
chunks.explain: He treated the animals differently from the other things.
chunks.st: whereas Rabbi Yehoshua made a distinction between them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Papias said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Papeyyas said:

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: I heard it like both of them:
chunks.st: I heard the statements of both of them applied to different situations:

chunks.en: if he clearly said his animals are hekdesh too,
chunks.st: One who consecrates all his possessions and explicitly
chunks.stMore: states that his animals are to be included, clearly intends to equate his animals with the rest of his possessions, that both should be consecrated for the same purpose, i.e., for Temple maintenance.

words.en: that the one who makes hekdesh

chunks.en: it is like the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: Therefore, he should act in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: And if he just said "my things,"
chunks.st: However, with regard to one who consecrates all his possessions without explicitly specifying that this includes his animals,
chunks.stMore: since there is no reason to presume that he wishes them all to be consecrated for the same purpose, it is presumed that each item is consecrated for the purpose most suited to it.

words.en: and the one who makes hekdesh

chunks.en: it is like the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.
chunks.st: Therefore, he should act in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua.

mishnayos.summary: If someone made all his things hekdesh, and among them were wine, oil and birds that could go on the mizbeach, they are sold, and the money buys olah korbanos.

chunks.en: If someone makes all his things hekdesh,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates all his possessions,

chunks.he: וְהָיוּ בָּהֶן דְּבָרִים רְאוּיִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: and among them are things fit for the mizbeach,
chunks.st: and among them there were items that are suitable to be sacrificed on the altar,

chunks.en: like wines, oils, and birds,
chunks.st: such as wines for libations, and oils for meal-offerings, and birds, e.g., turtledoves or young pigeons,

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: they are sold to people who need that kind of thing,
chunks.st: They are sold for the needs of that kind of item, i.e., to individuals who will use them as such.

chunks.en: and with their money he brings olah korbanos,
chunks.st: And he should bring with their monetary value that is received from their sale burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: and the rest of his things go to fix the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: And the rest of the possessions are allocated for Temple maintenance.

mishnayos.summary: Every thirty days the Beis HaMikdash set the price for flour, wine and oil. A seller always had to give hekdesh the better deal, and if his goods spoiled, he had the loss.

chunks.he: אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, מְשַׁעֲרִין אֶת הַלִּשְׁכָּה.
chunks.en: Once every thirty days they set the prices for the lishkah.
chunks.st: Once every thirty days, the prices at which the Temple supplies such as wine, flour, or oil will be purchased are set for the Temple chamber.

chunks.he: כָּל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו לְסַפֵּק סְלָתוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: Anyone who agrees to supply fine flour at four se'ah for a sela,
chunks.st: This set price is implemented in the following way: Any merchant who undertakes to provide fine flour after the chamber set a price of four se’a per sela,

chunks.en: if the price went up to three,
chunks.st: even if the general market price rose and stood at three se’a per sela,

chunks.en: must still supply at four.
chunks.st: he must provide fine flour based on the set price of four se’a per sela.

chunks.en: If he agreed at three and the price went down to four,
chunks.st: However, if the chamber’s set price was three se’a per sela, and the general market price fell to four se’a per sela,

chunks.en: he must supply at four,
chunks.st: he must now provide fine flour based on the new market price of four se’a per sela.

chunks.en: because hekdesh always has the upper hand.
chunks.st: This is in order that the Temple treasury of consecrated property always has the upper hand.

chunks.en: If the flour got wormy, it got wormy for him.
chunks.explain: The loss is his, and he must give new flour.
chunks.st: If the fine flour became wormy, it became wormy for the merchant,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he bears the loss of the ruined fine flour and must provide new fine flour in its place.

chunks.en: If the wine turned sour, it turned sour for him.
chunks.st: Similarly, if the wine turned to vinegar, it turned to vinegar for the merchant.

chunks.en: He does not get his money
chunks.st: This is because the merchant only receives, i.e., earns, his money

chunks.en: until the mizbeach accepts it.
chunks.explain: Only once it was brought as a korban.
chunks.st: once the altar is satisfied,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the transaction is only realized once the items have been sacrificed on the altar.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the people in charge of different jobs in the Beis HaMikdash, like the seals, the wine offerings, the lotteries, the gates, the music, the lechem hapanim and the ketores.

chunks.en: These are the people in charge in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: These are the officials who served in specific positions in the Temple:

chunks.en: Yochanan ben Pinchas was in charge of the seals,
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Pineḥas was responsible for the seals.
chunks.stMore: One who paid for a specific type of sacrificial item received a seal, which he presented to the Temple official in exchange for that item.

words.note: Tickets people bought to get the wine offerings for their korban.

chunks.en: Achiyah was in charge of the wine offerings,
chunks.st: Aḥiyya was responsible for the libations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the wine, oil, and flour prepared with the level of ritual purity necessary for the libation offerings and the meal-offerings, which accompanied many animal offerings. Aḥiyya supplied the libations to those who presented the appropriate seal.

chunks.en: Matisyah ben Shmuel was in charge of the lotteries,
chunks.st: Matya ben Shmuel was responsible for the lotteries,
chunks.stMore: which were used to select priests for the various Temple services each day.

words.note: Choosing which Kohen does each job.

chunks.en: Pesachyah was in charge of the bird pairs.
chunks.st: Petaḥya was responsible for the pairs of birds,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the turtledoves or pigeons, brought by a zav, a zava, a woman after childbirth, and a leper. They placed the appropriate sum of money into the horn designated for this purpose, and each day Petaḥya oversaw the purchase of birds from that money and their sacrifice in the proper manner.

chunks.en: Pesachyah is Mordechai.
chunks.st: Incidentally, the Gemara mentions: Petaḥya is Mordecai from the book of Esther.

words.note: Mordechai from the Megillah.

chunks.en: Why was he called Pesachyah?
chunks.st: And why was he called Petaḥya, which resembles the word for opening [petaḥ]?

chunks.en: Because he would open up hard topics and explain them,
chunks.st: The reason is that he would open, i.e., elucidate, difficult topics and interpret them to the people,

chunks.en: and he knew seventy languages.
chunks.st: and because he knew all seventy languages known at the time.

chunks.en: Ben Achiyah was in charge of Kohanim with stomach sickness,
chunks.st: The mishna resumes the list of officials. Ben Aḥiyya was responsible for the care of the priests who suffered from intestinal disease.

chunks.en: Nechunya dug wells,
chunks.st: Neḥunya was the well digger for pilgrims on their way to Jerusalem for the Festivals.

words.note: Wells for people coming to Yerushalayim for Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Gevini was the caller,
chunks.st: Gevini was the Temple crier
chunks.stMore: who would awaken the priests and the Levites for their Temple duties.

words.note: He called out to wake the Kohanim and Levi'im for their work.

chunks.en: Ben Gever was in charge of locking the gates,
chunks.st: Ben Gever was responsible for locking the Temple gates in the evening and for unlocking them in the morning.

chunks.en: Ben Bevai was in charge of the wicks,
chunks.st: Ben Bevai was appointed over the shreds of garments,
chunks.stMore: which were formed into wicks for the Temple candelabra. He also supervised the twisting of those wicks into the appropriate thickness for the various nights during the different seasons of the year.

words.note: Made from old clothes of the Kohanim, for the Menorah.

chunks.en: Ben Arza was in charge of the cymbal,
chunks.st: Ben Arza was responsible for the cymbal,
chunks.stMore: which was rung as a signal that the Levites should commence their song.

words.note: A metal musical instrument, rung so the Levi'im would start to sing.

chunks.en: Hugras ben Levi was in charge of the singing,
chunks.st: Hugras ben Levi was responsible for the song. He taught and conducted the singers in the Temple.

chunks.he: בֵּית גַּרְמוּ עַל מַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
chunks.en: the family of Garmu was in charge of making the lechem hapanim,
chunks.st: The house of Garmu was responsible for the preparation of the shewbread;

chunks.en: the family of Avtinas was in charge of making the ketores,
chunks.st: the house of Avtinas was responsible for the preparation of the incense;

chunks.en: Elazar was in charge of the curtains,
chunks.st: and Elazar was responsible for weaving the Temple curtains;

chunks.en: and Pinchas was in charge of the clothing.
chunks.explain: He helped the Kohanim get dressed in their special clothes.
chunks.st: and Pineḥas was the valet,
chunks.stMore: who assisted the priests in fitting their clothes and dressing themselves for their Temple service.

mishnayos.summary: There must be at least three treasurers and seven trustees for the money of the Beis HaMikdash. People in charge of public money must be at least two, except for two special people everyone trusted.

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁלֹשָה גִּזְבָּרִין וּמִשִּׁבְעָה אֲמַרְכָּלִין,
chunks.en: There may not be fewer than three treasurers and seven trustees.
chunks.st: There must be no fewer than seven trustees [amarkolin] and three treasurers appointed over the Temple administration.

chunks.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין שְׂרָרָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר בְּמָמוֹן
chunks.en: And we do not make someone in charge of public money
chunks.st: And we do not appoint an authority over the public comprised

chunks.en: with less than two people,
chunks.st: of fewer than two people,

chunks.he: חוּץ מִבֶּן אֲחִיָּה שֶׁעַל חוֹלֵי מֵעַיִם
chunks.en: except for Ben Achiyah, who was in charge of stomach sickness,
chunks.st: except for ben Aḥiyya, who was responsible for healing priests who suffered from intestinal disease,

chunks.en: and Elazar, who was in charge of the curtains,
chunks.st: and Elazar, who was responsible for the weaving of the Temple curtains.

chunks.en: because most of the people accepted them.
chunks.st: The reason for these exceptions is that the majority of the public accepted these men upon themselves
chunks.stMore: as officials who served without the assistance of even a single partner.

mishnayos.summary: There were seals with words written on them, each for a different kind of wine offering. This mishnah tells what was written on them and which korbanos each one was for.

chunks.en: There were four seals in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: There were four seals in the Temple
chunks.stMore: that confirmed that the bearer had paid for the libations that accompanied his offering.

chunks.en: and on them was written,
chunks.st: And one of the following inscriptions was written on them:

chunks.en: "Calf," "Male,"
chunks.st: Calf; male, i.e., a ram;

words.note: Here it means a ram.

chunks.en: "Kid," "Sinner."
chunks.st: kid; and sinner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a leper, as leprosy is a punishment for one of seven sins (see Arakhin 16a). Conversely,

words.note: A young goat.
Here it means a metzora, a person with tzaraas.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says,
chunks.st: ben Azzai says:

chunks.en: There were five,
chunks.st: There were five seals,

chunks.en: and written on them in Aramaic was:
chunks.st: and the following was written upon them in Aramaic, not Hebrew:

chunks.he: עֵגֶל, זָכָר, גְּדִי, חוֹטֵא דַּל, וְחוֹטֵא עָשִׁיר.
chunks.en: "Calf," "Male," "Kid," "Poor sinner," and "Rich sinner."
chunks.st: Calf, male, kid, poor sinner, and rich sinner.

chunks.en: The "Calf" seal is used for the wine offerings of cattle,
chunks.st: The mishna explains the significance of each of the four aforementioned seals. The calf seal serves as a payment receipt for libations of cattle offerings,

chunks.en: big or small, male or female.
chunks.st: whether they are large or small, male or female,
chunks.stMore: as all offerings from the cow family are accompanied by the same libation.

chunks.en: The "Kid" seal is used for the wine offerings of sheep and goats,
chunks.st: The kid seal serves for libations of sheep or goat offerings,

chunks.en: big or small, male or female,
chunks.st: whether large or small, male or female,

chunks.en: except for rams.
chunks.st: except for those of rams aged thirteen months and older.

chunks.he: זָכָר מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם נִסְכֵּי אֵילִים בִּלְבָד.
chunks.en: The "Male" seal is used only for the wine offerings of rams.
chunks.st: The ram seal, which was earlier called the male seal, serves exclusively for ram libations.

chunks.en: The "Sinner" seal is used for the wine offerings
chunks.st: The sinner seal serves for libations of the

chunks.en: of the three animals of a metzora.
chunks.explain: A metzora brings three animals when he becomes tahor.
chunks.st: three animal offerings of a leper, for the completion of his purification.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna provides details of the functions performed by Yoḥanan ben Pineḥas and Aḥiyya, the officials mentioned in the first mishna of this chapter, which concerns the seals and libations.

mishnayos.summary: To get wine offerings, a person paid Yochanan for a seal and gave the seal to Achiyah. In the evening they checked the money against the seals, and hekdesh always came out ahead.

chunks.en: Someone who wants wine offerings
chunks.st: One who seeks libations for his offering

chunks.en: goes to Yochanan,
chunks.st: goes to Yoḥanan,

chunks.en: who is in charge of the seals,
chunks.st: the official who was responsible for the seals,

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן לוֹ מָעוֹת וּמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ חוֹתָם.
chunks.en: gives him money, and gets a seal from him.
chunks.st: and gives him the appropriate sum of money and receives a seal from him.

chunks.en: Then he comes to Achiyah,
chunks.st: With that seal he subsequently comes to Aḥiyya,

chunks.en: who is in charge of the wine offerings,
chunks.st: who was responsible for the libations,

chunks.he: וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ חוֹתָם וּמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ נְסָכִים.
chunks.en: and gives him the seal and gets the wine offerings from him.
chunks.st: and gives him Yoḥanan’s seal and receives his libations from him.

chunks.en: In the evening they meet each other,
chunks.st: In the evening, Yoḥanan and Aḥiyya would get together to reconcile their accounts,

chunks.en: and Achiyah takes out the seals
chunks.st: and Aḥiyya would take out the seals he had received

chunks.en: and gets money in their place.
chunks.st: and accept the money Yoḥanan had received in exchange for them.

chunks.he: וְאִם הוֹתִירוּ הוֹתִירוּ לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ. וְאִם פָּחָתוּ,
chunks.en: If there was extra, the extra goes to hekdesh. But if there was too little,
chunks.st: If the money was less than the value of the seals, they were less to him, i.e., Yoḥanan would bear the loss,

chunks.en: Yochanan would pay from his own house,
chunks.st: and Yoḥanan would have to pay the difference to the Temple treasury from his own property. And if there was some money left over, i.e., the total money was greater than the value of the seals, they were left over to the benefit of the Temple treasury of consecrated property,

chunks.en: because hekdesh always has the upper hand.
chunks.st: as the Temple treasury always has the upper hand.

mishnayos.summary: If someone lost his seal, they waited until evening to see if there was extra money for it. The day was written on the seals so cheaters could not use old ones.

chunks.en: Someone who lost his seal
chunks.st: With regard to one who lost his seal that he purchased from Yoḥanan,

chunks.en: they wait for him until evening.
chunks.st: Yoḥanan and Aḥiyya would wait to resolve his problem until the evening.

chunks.en: If they find extra money worth his seal,
chunks.st: And when they added their accounts in the evening, if they found for him a surplus of money equivalent to the value of his seal,

chunks.en: they give him the wine offerings.
chunks.st: they would give him the corresponding libations.

chunks.en: And if not, he gets nothing.
chunks.st: And if not, they would not give him libations.

chunks.he: וְשֵׁם הַיּוֹם כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן מִפְּנֵי הָרַמָּאִין:
chunks.en: The name of the day was written on them because of cheaters.
chunks.explain: So no one could use an old seal from another day.
chunks.st: And the name of the day of the week was written upon the seals because of the cheats.
chunks.stMore: They might try to use old seals that had been lost by the Temple officials or by someone who had brought an offering at an earlier date, so as to receive libations in a deceitful manner.
