mishnayos.summary: There were two special rooms in the Beis HaMikdash. In one, people secretly gave tzedakah for poor people from good families, and in the other, people gave vessels to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: There were two rooms in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: There were two special chambers in the Temple,

chunks.en: one was the secret room,
chunks.st: one called the chamber of secret gifts

chunks.en: and one was the room of vessels.
chunks.st: and the other one called the chamber of vessels.

chunks.en: In the secret room, people who fear sin
chunks.st: The mishna explains the purpose of these chambers. In the chamber of secret gifts, sin-fearing people

chunks.en: put money in it secretly,
chunks.st: put money secretly

chunks.he: וַעֲנִיִּים בְּנֵי טוֹבִים מִתְפַּרְנְסִים מִתוֹכָהּ בַּחֲשַׁאי.
chunks.en: and poor people from good families get their support from it secretly.
chunks.explain: So no one would be embarrassed.
chunks.st: and poor people of noble descent support themselves from it secretly.

chunks.en: The room of vessels:
chunks.st: With regard to the chamber of vessels,

chunks.he: כָּל מִי שֶׁהוּא מִתְנַדֵּב כֶּלִי, זוֹרְקוֹ לְתוֹכָהּ.
chunks.en: whoever gives a vessel as a gift throws it inside.
chunks.st: anyone who donates a vessel to the Temple drops it inside that chamber,

chunks.he: וְאַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, גִּזְבָּרִין פּוֹתְחִין אוֹתָהּ.
chunks.en: Once every thirty days the treasurers open it.
chunks.st: and once every thirty days the treasurers open it.

chunks.he: וְכָל כְּלִי שֶׁמּוֹצְאִין בּוֹ צֹרֶךְ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: Any vessel they find useful for fixing the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: And any vessel that they found for it a use for Temple maintenance,

chunks.en: they keep it.
chunks.st: they leave it for that purpose,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר נִמְכָּרִין בִּדְמֵיהֶן וְנוֹפְלִין לְלִשְׁכַּת בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת:
chunks.en: The rest are sold, and their money goes to the room for fixing the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: and the rest are sold, and their monetary value is allocated to Temple maintenance.

mishnayos.summary: There were thirteen collection boxes, thirteen tables and thirteen places to bow in the Beis HaMikdash. Two families bowed in a fourteenth place, where they had a tradition that the Aron was hidden.

chunks.en: Thirteen collection boxes,
chunks.st: There were thirteen collection horns, narrow at the top and wide at the bottom,
chunks.stMore: into which were placed the shekels that were collected for the various needs of the Temple.

words.note: Collection boxes shaped like a ram's horn.

chunks.en: thirteen tables,
chunks.st: There were also thirteen tables for various purposes,

chunks.en: and thirteen places to bow down were in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: and thirteen prostrations in the Temple.

chunks.en: The family of Rabban Gamliel
chunks.st: The members of the household of Rabban Gamliel

chunks.he: וְשֶׁל בֵּית רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים
chunks.en: and the family of Rabbi Chananya, the assistant Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and the members of the household of Rabbi Ḥananya, the deputy High Priest,

chunks.en: would bow down fourteen times.
chunks.st: would prostrate themselves in fourteen places.

chunks.en: Where was the extra one?
chunks.st: And where was this extra location?

chunks.en: Facing the woodshed,
chunks.st: It was facing the wood depository,

chunks.en: because they had a tradition from their fathers
chunks.st: as there was a tradition handed down to them from their fathers

chunks.en: that the Aron was hidden there.
chunks.st: that the Ark was sequestered there.

words.note: The Aron with the Luchos, the holy box from the Mishkan.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen once saw that one floor stone was different from the others. He started to tell his friend but passed away before he could finish, and then they knew for sure that the Aron was hidden there.

chunks.en: Once there was a Kohen who was busy with his work,
chunks.st: an incident involving a certain priest who was going about his duties

chunks.en: and he saw a floor stone that was different from the others.
chunks.st: and saw a certain flagstone that was different from the others.
chunks.stMore: He noticed that one of the stones was slightly raised above the others, indicating that it had been removed and returned to its place. The priest understood that this was the opening to an underground tunnel where the Ark was concealed.

chunks.en: He came and told his friend.
chunks.st: He came and said to his fellow that he had noticed this deviation in the floor.

chunks.en: He did not get to finish telling it
chunks.st: He did not manage to conclude relating the incident

chunks.en: before he passed away,
chunks.st: before his soul left him, i.e., he died.

chunks.en: and they knew for sure that the Aron was hidden there.
chunks.st: Following this event, they knew with certainty that the Ark was sequestered there
chunks.stMore: and that God had prevented that priest from revealing its location.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna relates that there was

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells where the thirteen places to bow were: facing the thirteen gates of the Azarah. It names the gates and tells why some of them got their names.

chunks.en: Where did they bow down?
chunks.st: Where were these prostrations?

chunks.en: Four in the north, and four in the south,
chunks.st: There were four in the north of the courtyard, four in the south,

chunks.en: three in the east, and two in the west,
chunks.st: three in the east and two in the west,

chunks.en: facing the thirteen gates.
chunks.st: as the thirteen prostrations were facing the thirteen gates of the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: The gates in the south, starting near the west, were:
chunks.st: The thirteen gates were as follows: The southern ones, listed in order, beginning with the one adjacent to the western side, were

chunks.en: the Upper Gate,
chunks.st: the Upper Gate,
chunks.stMore: and the topography of the courtyard was such that there was an incline on the east-west plane, therefore the gate farthest to the west was higher than the other gates;

chunks.en: the Gate of Kindling,
chunks.st: the Gate of Kindling,
chunks.stMore: through which the priests would bring the wood for the arrangement of fire on top of the altar;

words.note: The wood for the fire on the mizbeach came through it.

chunks.en: the Gate of the Firstborn,
chunks.st: the Gate of the Firstborn,
chunks.stMore: through which priests would bring the ritually pure firstborn animals to be sacrificed, as it is permitted to slaughter firstborn animals on the southern side of the courtyard;

chunks.en: and the Gate of Water.
chunks.st: and the Gate of Water.

chunks.en: Why was it called the Gate of Water?
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: And why was it named the Gate of Water?

chunks.en: Because through it they brought in a jug
chunks.st: Since through it they would bring in the vial of

chunks.en: of water for pouring on the mizbeach on Sukkos.
chunks.st: water for the water libation on the festival of Sukkot,
chunks.stMore: as they would ceremoniously draw the water from the Pool of Siloam and bring it to the altar through this gate.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: There was a different reason for this name.

chunks.en: through it the water trickles,
chunks.st: It was called the Gate of Water because through it the water would trickle [mefakim],

chunks.he: וַעֲתִידִין לִהְיוֹת יוֹצְאִין מִתַּחַת מִפְתַּן הַבַּיִת.
chunks.en: and one day it will flow out from under the doorstep of the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: and in the future this water will increase and go out from under the threshold of the House.

chunks.en: Across from them in the north, starting near the west:
chunks.st: Facing these gates were the ones in the north, listed in order from the one closest to the west:

chunks.en: the Gate of Yechanyah,
chunks.st: The Gate of Jeconiah;

words.note: A king of Yehudah.

chunks.en: the Gate of the Korban,
chunks.st: the Gate of the Offering,
chunks.stMore: through which they would bring the offerings of the most sacred order, as these could be slaughtered only in the northern part of the courtyard;

chunks.en: the Gate of Women,
chunks.st: the Gate of Women,
chunks.stMore: where women would enter the courtyard to place their hands on the heads of their offerings;

chunks.en: and the Gate of Song.
chunks.st: and the Gate of Song,
chunks.stMore: through which they would bring the musical instruments into the courtyard.

words.note: The Levi'im brought their instruments through it.

chunks.en: Why was it called the Gate of Yechanyah?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: And why was it called the Gate of Jeconiah?

chunks.en: Because through it Yechanyah went out to galus.
chunks.st: The reason is that through it Jeconiah went out to his exile.
chunks.stMore: Before Jeconiah was exiled by Nebuchadnezzar to Babylon he came to take leave of the Temple, and he left through this gate.

chunks.en: In the east was the Gate of Nikanor,
chunks.st: The mishna resumes the list with the gates that are in the east: the Gate of Nicanor, which was named after Nicanor,
chunks.stMore: who brought the doors of this gate from Egypt (see Yoma 38a).

words.note: A man who brought its doors from Egypt.

chunks.en: and it had two small doors,
chunks.st: And the Gate of Nicanor had two wickets [pishpeshin],

chunks.en: one on its right and one on its left.
chunks.st: one on its right and one on its left.

chunks.he: וּשְׁנַיִם בַּמַּעֲרָב שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם שֵׁם:
chunks.en: And there were two in the west that had no name.
chunks.st: And there were two gates in the west that did not have a name, making a total of thirteen gates.

mishnayos.stIntro: The previous mishna mentioned that there were thirteen prostrations in the Temple.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells where the thirteen tables in the Beis HaMikdash stood and what each was used for. We always go up in holiness and never down.

chunks.en: There were thirteen tables in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: There were thirteen tables in the Temple.

chunks.en: Eight were marble, in the place where the animals were shechted,
chunks.st: Eight of them were made of marble and were located in the slaughtering area, north of the altar,
chunks.stMore: where the priests would slaughter the offerings of the most sacred order.

chunks.en: and on them they washed the insides of the korbanos.
chunks.st: Upon these tables they would wash the innards of the offerings,
chunks.stMore: as the marble was cool and preserved the freshness of the meat.

chunks.en: And two were on the west side of the ramp,
chunks.st: And there were two more tables on the western side of the ramp, south of the altar,

words.note: The ramp going up to the mizbeach.

chunks.he: אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל כֶּסֶף
chunks.en: one of marble and one of silver.
chunks.st: one of marble and one of silver.

chunks.he: עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ הָיוּ נוֹתְנִים אֶת הָאֵבָרִים,
chunks.en: On the marble one they put the parts of the korban,
chunks.st: On the table of marble they would place the limbs before they were sacrificed,
chunks.stMore: and from there the priests would bring them up to the altar.

chunks.en: on the silver one, the vessels used for the avodah.
chunks.st: On the table made of silver they would place the ninety-three sacred vessels
chunks.stMore: brought out from the Chamber of Vessels each morning for the services of that day.

chunks.he: וּשְׁנַיִם בָּאוּלָם מִבִּפְנִים עַל פֶּתַח הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: And two were inside the Ulam, near the door of the Heichal,
chunks.st: And there were two tables in the Entrance Hall to the Sanctuary, on the inside of the Entrance Hall, near the opening to the Temple,

words.note: The front hall of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב,
chunks.en: one of marble and one of gold.
chunks.st: one of marble and one of gold.

chunks.he: עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ נוֹתְנִין לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ,
chunks.en: On the marble one they put the lechem hapanim when it is brought in,
chunks.st: On the table of marble they would put the shewbread before its entrance to the Sanctuary after it was baked on the eve of Shabbat.

chunks.en: and on the gold one when it is taken out,
chunks.st: And they would place the old shewbread on the table of gold upon its exit from the Sanctuary, to be divided among the priests.

chunks.en: because we go up in holiness and not down.
chunks.explain: It was on a gold table inside, so it cannot go onto marble.
chunks.st: The reason the shewbread was placed on a marble table before being brought into the Sanctuary and on a golden one upon when removed from there is that one elevates to a higher level in matters of sanctity and one does not downgrade.
chunks.stMore: Since it had been placed on the golden Shewbread table all week inside the Sanctuary, upon its removal it could not be derogated to a marble table and so was placed on a different golden table in the Entrance Hall.

chunks.en: And one of gold was inside,
chunks.st: Finally, there was one table of gold inside the Sanctuary, i.e. the Shewbread table,

chunks.en: on which the lechem hapanim always lay.
chunks.st: upon which the shewbread was placed always.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna details the exact location and purpose of the thirteen tables in the Temple.

mishnayos.summary: There were thirteen collection boxes in the Beis HaMikdash, each with a label telling what its money was for. Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages argue about the boxes for birds.

chunks.he: שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר שׁוֹפָרוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְכָתוּב עֲלֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: There were thirteen collection boxes in the Beis HaMikdash, and on them was written:
chunks.st: There were thirteen collection horns in the Temple, and the intended use of the funds was written upon each one, as follows:

chunks.en: "New shekels" and "Old shekels,"
chunks.st: New shekels, old shekels,

chunks.en: "Bird pairs" and "Young birds for an olah,"
chunks.st: pairs of birds, fledglings designated for burnt-offerings,

chunks.en: "Wood," "Levonah,"
chunks.st: wood for the arrangement on the altar, frankincense that accompanied meal-offerings,

words.note: A sweet-smelling spice put with a mincha.

chunks.en: "Gold for the kapores."
chunks.st: and gold donated for the Ark cover.

words.note: The gold cover on top of the Aron.

chunks.en: Six were for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: The remaining six horns were designated for communal free-will offerings.

chunks.en: "New shekels" is for the half-shekel of each year.
chunks.st: The horn labeled new shekels was designated for the half-shekel donation that was brought every year for the needs of that year.

chunks.en: "Old": whoever did not give his half-shekel last year
chunks.st: The horn labeled old shekels was for one who did not bring his half-shekel the previous year,

chunks.en: gives it for the next year.
chunks.st: who would contribute his shekel for the following year.

chunks.en: "Bird pairs" are turtledoves.
chunks.st: The funds in the horn labeled pairs of birds are designated for the turtledoves used for bird-offerings,

chunks.en: "Young birds for an olah" are young pigeons.
chunks.st: and the one labeled fledglings for burnt-offerings are used to purchase young pigeons as burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: And they are all olah korbanos.
chunks.st: All of these, i.e., the funds in both horns, were used exclusively for voluntary burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehuda says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: "Bird pairs" are one chatas and one olah.
chunks.st: The funds in both the horn labeled pairs of birds and the horn labeled fledglings were for young pigeons and turtledoves. The distinction between them is that the funds in the horn labeled pairs of birds were designated for the obligatory offerings of a zav, a zava, a woman after childbirth, and a leper. These offerings included a pair of birds, one brought for a sin-offering, and the other one brought for a burnt-offering.

chunks.en: "Young birds for an olah" are all olah korbanos.
chunks.st: Conversely, the funds in the horn labeled fledglings for burnt-offerings were all used exclusively for voluntary burnt-offerings.

mishnayos.summary: If someone promises wood, levonah or gold, there is a smallest amount he must give. Extra money for a chatas or asham buys olah korbanos, so that both pesukim come true.

chunks.en: If someone says, "I promise to give wood,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate wood to the Temple,

chunks.en: he must give no less than two logs.
chunks.st: must donate no fewer than two logs for the arrangement on the altar.

chunks.en: Levonah, no less than a handful.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate frankincense, must donate no less than a handful of frankincense, the amount brought with a meal-offering.

chunks.en: Gold, no less than a gold dinar.
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate gold, must donate no less than a dinar of gold.

chunks.en: "Six boxes for gift korbanos."
chunks.st: It was stated that six horns were designated for communal free-will offerings.

chunks.en: What did they do with the gift money?
chunks.st: The Mishna asks: With regard to the money designated for communal free-will offerings, what would they do with this money?

chunks.en: They bought olah korbanos with it.
chunks.st: The Mishna answers that they used it to purchase animals for burnt-offerings,

chunks.en: The meat is for Hashem, and the skins are for the Kohanim.
chunks.st: as the meat from these offerings was offered on the altar to God and the hides were given to the priests.

chunks.he: זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ יְהוֹיָדָע כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
chunks.en: Yehoyada the Kohen Gadol taught this explanation:
chunks.st: This midrash was taught by Jehoiada the High Priest: There is an apparent contradiction between two verses.

chunks.he: (ויקרא ה) אָשָׁם הוּא אָשֹׁם אָשַׁם לַיְיָ.
chunks.en: "It is an asham; he is guilty to Hashem."
chunks.explain: But another pasuk says the asham goes to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: With regard to the guilt-offering, the verse states: “It is a guilt-offering; he is certainly guilty before the Lord”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 5:19). This verse indicates that the guilt-offering goes to God, not the priests. However, a different verse states: “As is the sin-offering, so is the guilt-offering; there is one law for them; the priest who makes atonement with it, he shall have it” (Leviticus 7:7). This verse indicates that the offering is designated for the priests alone. How can these two verses be reconciled? The Mishna explains that

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: this is the principle:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא בָּא מִשּׁוּם חֵטְא וּמִשּׁוּם אַשְׁמָה,
chunks.en: Any money that comes because of a chatas or an asham
chunks.st: Any funds that come due to a sin-offering or due to a guilt-offering, i.e., leftover coins designated for one of these offerings,

chunks.en: buys olah korbanos.
chunks.st: they should be used for the purchase of animals for a voluntary burnt-offering,

chunks.en: The meat is for Hashem, and the skins are for the Kohanim.
chunks.st: as the meat will be offered on the altar to God, and the hides will go to the priests.

chunks.en: So both pesukim come true:
chunks.st: In this manner the two verses are found to be fulfilled,

chunks.en: an asham for Hashem and an asham for the Kohanim.
chunks.st: as it is both a guilt-offering to God as well as a guilt-offering to the priest.

chunks.en: And it says,
chunks.st: And this halakha also explains the verse that says:

chunks.en: "Asham money and chatas money
chunks.st: “The guilt-offering money and the sin-offering money

chunks.he: לֹא יוּבָא בֵּית ה' לַכֹּהֲנִים יִהְיוּ:
chunks.en: was not brought into the house of Hashem; it shall be for the Kohanim."
chunks.st: was not brought into the House of the Lord; it was for the priests”
chunks.stMore: (II Kings 12:17). This verse is understood to refer to the hides given to the priests.

mishnayos.summary: If coins are found on the floor between two collection boxes, they go to the closer box. If they are right in the middle, they go to the box with the stricter rule.

chunks.en: Coins found between the shekalim box and the gift box:
chunks.st: If money was found on the floor of the Temple between one of the collection horns marked shekels and the collection horn marked free-will offerings, that is to say,
chunks.stMore: between the first and the thirteenth collection horns, in which funds contributed to the Temple were stored, the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if closer to the shekalim, they go to the shekalim;
chunks.st: If the money was found closer to the horn marked shekels, it is allocated to the shekels;

chunks.en: if closer to the gift box, they go to the gift box;
chunks.st: if it was found closer to the horn marked free-will offerings, it is allocated to free-will offerings;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, they go to the gift box.
chunks.st: and if it was equidistant from the horn marked shekels and the horn marked free-will offerings, it is allocated to free-will offerings.

chunks.en: Between the wood box and the levonah box:
chunks.st: If the money was found between the horn marked wood and the horn marked frankincense, that is, between the fifth and sixth horns,

chunks.en: if closer to the wood, they go to the wood;
chunks.st: if it was closer to the horn marked wood, it is allocated to wood;

chunks.en: if closer to the levonah, they go to the levonah;
chunks.st: if it was closer to the horn marked frankincense, it is allocated to frankincense;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, they go to the levonah.
chunks.st: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to frankincense.

chunks.en: Between the bird pairs box and the young birds for an olah box:
chunks.st: If the money was found between the horn marked pairs of bird-offerings and the horn marked doves for burnt-offerings, i.e., between the third and the fourth horns,

chunks.en: if closer to the bird pairs, they go to the bird pairs;
chunks.st: if it is closer to the horn marked pairs of bird-offerings, it is allocated to pairs of bird-offerings;

chunks.en: if closer to the young birds for an olah, they go there;
chunks.st: if it was found closer to the horn marked doves for burnt-offerings, it is allocated to doves for burnt-offerings;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, they go to the young birds for an olah.
chunks.st: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to doves for burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: Between plain money and maaser sheni money:
chunks.st: And similarly, if money was found anywhere else between a container for ordinary, non-sacred money and one containing second-tithe money, the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if closer to the plain money, it is plain money;
chunks.st: If the money was found closer to the non-sacred money, it is allocated to the non-sacred money;

chunks.en: if closer to maaser sheni, it is maaser sheni;
chunks.st: if it was found closer to second-tithe money, it is allocated to second-tithe money;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, it is maaser sheni.
chunks.st: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to second-tithe money.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: we follow what is closer, even to be lenient,
chunks.st: In cases of doubt, the ruling follows whichever is closer, even if this involves being lenient,

chunks.en: and if right in the middle, we are strict.
chunks.st: but if the money was found equidistant from both, the ruling follows whichever allocation involves being stringent.

mishnayos.summary: When we find coins and don't know whose they are, we decide by where and when they were found. Near the animal sellers, or in Yerushalayim on Yom Tov, they are counted as maaser sheni money.

chunks.en: Coins found near the animal sellers
chunks.explain: In Yerushalayim, people bought animals with maaser sheni money.
chunks.st: Money found before animal merchants in Jerusalem

chunks.en: are always maaser sheni.
chunks.st: is always presumed to be second-tithe money.
chunks.stMore: The presumption is based on the fact that in Jerusalem, most of the animals are bought with second-tithe money and sacrificed as peace-offerings.

chunks.en: On Har HaBayis, they are plain money.
chunks.st: And money found on the Temple Mount is presumed to be non-sacred money.

chunks.en: In Yerushalayim at the time of Yom Tov, they are maaser sheni,
chunks.st: And with regard to money found in the rest of Jerusalem, the following distinction applies:

chunks.en: and the rest of the year, they are plain money.
chunks.st: If it was found during the rest of the days of the year, it is presumed to be non-sacred money, but if it was found during the time of a pilgrim Festival, it is all presumed to be second-tithe money,
chunks.stMore: because most of the money found in Jerusalem at the time of a Festival is second-tithe money.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna considers other situations in which something is found and its source is unknown.

mishnayos.summary: If meat is found in the Azarah or in Yerushalayim, we decide what kind of korban it probably is, and it must be burned. Meat found outside Yerushalayim may sometimes be eaten.

chunks.en: Meat that was found in the Azarah:
chunks.st: The mishna continues: With regard to meat that was found in the Temple courtyard,
chunks.stMore: and it is not known from whence it came, the halakha is as follows:

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: whole parts are olah korbanos,
chunks.st: If it is whole limbs of the animal, in the manner that burnt-offerings are brought to the altar, it is presumed to be burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: and small pieces are chataos.
chunks.st: And if it is in small pieces, it is presumed to be sin-offerings.

chunks.en: In Yerushalayim, it is shelamim.
chunks.st: And if the meat, in whatever form, is found in the city of Jerusalem, as opposed to the courtyard, it is presumed to be the meat of peace-offerings,
chunks.stMore: as most of the meat in Jerusalem is the meat of peace-offerings.

chunks.en: Either way, it is left until it spoils
chunks.explain: Maybe its time to be eaten has passed already.
chunks.st: Since it is possible that the time during which it is permitted to eat any of it has already passed, both this and that, whether it is determined to be the meat of burnt-offerings or the meat of peace-offerings, its form must be allowed to decay, i.e., it must be left until it is definitely disqualified,

chunks.en: and it is taken out to the place for burning.
chunks.st: and then it must be taken out to the place of burning, where offerings that have become disqualified are burned.

chunks.en: If it was found outside Yerushalayim:
chunks.st: With regard to meat found in the outlying areas, outside of Jerusalem,

chunks.en: whole parts are neveilos, not kosher,
chunks.st: if it is in the form of whole limbs, the meat presumably comes from carcasses
chunks.stMore: of animals that were not properly slaughtered, for meat unfit for eating was generally cut up into full limbs, to be fed to dogs or sold to gentiles.

words.note: Animals that died without shechitah, which may not be eaten.

chunks.en: and small pieces are allowed.
chunks.st: But if it is in small pieces, it is presumably kosher and permitted to be eaten,
chunks.stMore: as kosher meat was ordinarily cut up into small pieces.

chunks.en: And at Yom Tov time, when there is lots of meat,
chunks.st: And if meat is found at the time of a Festival, when meat is plentiful, so that it is generally not cut up into small pieces,

chunks.en: even whole parts are allowed.
chunks.st: then even whole limbs are permitted to be eaten.

mishnayos.summary: An animal found near Yerushalayim is probably a korban. Males are counted as olah korbanos and females as shelamim, and Rabbi Yehuda adds a rule for the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: An animal that was found
chunks.st: If an animal that is fit for the altar was found straying,

chunks.en: from Yerushalayim up to Migdal Eder,
chunks.st: from Jerusalem and as far as Migdal Eder,

words.note: A place near Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: or the same distance in any direction:
chunks.st: and similarly if it was found within that distance from Jerusalem in any other direction,
chunks.stMore: it is presumed that the animal came from Jerusalem. Most of the animals in Jerusalem were designated for offerings, and presumably this one was as well.

chunks.en: males are olah korbanos,
chunks.st: Males are presumed to be burnt-offerings, as only males are brought as burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: females are shelamim.
chunks.st: Females are presumed to be peace-offerings, as it is permitted to bring a female peace-offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: One that is fit for a korban Pesach
chunks.st: An animal that is fit for the Paschal offering, i.e., a one-year-old male lamb or kid,

chunks.en: is a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: is presumed to be a Paschal offering,

chunks.en: if it is within thirty days before Pesach.
chunks.st: provided that it was found within thirty days before the Festival of Passover.

mishnayos.summary: At first, a person who found such an animal had to pay for its wine offerings, so people stopped taking the animals. So beis din made a rule that the community pays for them.

chunks.en: At first they would take a pledge from the one who found it,
chunks.st: Originally, the court would seize collateral from one who found such an animal,

chunks.en: until he brings its wine offerings.
chunks.st: as security until he would bring with it the libations associated with this offering,
chunks.stMore: as if the found animal were his own and he had committed himself to bring the libations.

chunks.en: Then people began to leave it and run away.
chunks.st: This brought about a situation in which those who found the animals began leaving them where they found them, and absconding, so as not to become liable for the libations.

chunks.en: Beis din made a rule
chunks.st: The court therefore instituted that the libations accompanying these offerings

chunks.en: that its wine offerings come from the money of the community.
chunks.st: would come from public funds, that is, from the Temple treasury.

mishnayos.summary: Beis din made seven rules about korbanos. This mishnah tells some of them: when the community pays for wine offerings, and for the mincha of a Kohen Gadol who passed away.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: Beis din made seven rules,
chunks.st: The court instituted seven ordinances
chunks.stMore: with regard to the financial aspects of offerings and consecrations.

chunks.en: and this is one of them.
chunks.st: And this ordinance, namely, that the cost of the libations accompanying the sacrifice of a found animal is borne by the public, is one of them.

chunks.en: A non-Jew who sent his olah from far away
chunks.st: These are the other ordinances: If a gentile sent his burnt-offering from abroad, outside Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and sent wine offerings with it,
chunks.st: and he sent with it money for the purchase of the libations that must accompany it,

chunks.en: they are brought from his money.
chunks.st: the libations are offered at his expense.

chunks.en: And if not, they are brought from the money of the community.
chunks.st: And if the gentile did not cover the cost of the libations, it is a condition of the court that the libations are sacrificed at the public’s expense, with funds taken from the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: And also a ger who passed away and left korbanos:
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of a convert who died without heirs and left animals that he had designated as offerings.

chunks.en: if he has wine offerings,
chunks.st: If he has the libations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if he also had set aside libations or money for that purpose,

chunks.en: they are brought from his.
chunks.st: the libations are sacrificed from his estate.

chunks.en: And if not, they are brought from the money of the community.
chunks.st: And if he did not do so, the libations are sacrificed from public funds.

chunks.en: And it is a rule of beis din
chunks.st: And another ordinance: It is a condition of the court

chunks.en: about a Kohen Gadol who passed away,
chunks.st: with regard to a High Priest who died,
chunks.stMore: and a new High Priest had not yet been appointed in his place,

chunks.en: that his mincha is brought from the money of the community.
chunks.st: that his meal-offering, i.e., the griddle-cake offering that the High Priest would bring each day from one-tenth of an ephah of flour, would be sacrificed from public funds.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol brought a flour korban every day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: from the money of his family.
chunks.st: It was brought from the property of the High Priest’s heirs, i.e., his estate, and not from public funds.

chunks.en: And it was brought whole.
chunks.explain: All of it at once, not half in the morning and half at night.
chunks.st: In any event, the offering was not brought as it would have been brought by the High Priest himself were he still alive, half in the morning and half in the evening, but rather it was sacrificed all at once, from a whole one-tenth of an ephah.

mishnayos.summary: More of beis din's rules: the Kohanim may use the salt and wood, using the parah adumah's ashes is not me'ilah, and the community pays for birds that became pasul.

chunks.en: About the salt
chunks.st: The fourth ordinance was about the salt in the Temple that was designated for salting the offerings,

words.note: Salt that was put on the korbanos.

chunks.en: and about the wood,
chunks.st: and the fifth was about the wood that was used for the burning of the offerings.

chunks.en: that the Kohanim may use them,
chunks.explain: To cook the meat of the korbanos they eat.
chunks.st: These ordinances decreed that the priests may use them also to prepare the meat of the offerings that they eat.

chunks.he: וְעַל הַפָּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מוֹעֲלִין בְּאֶפְרָהּ,
chunks.en: and about the parah adumah, that using its ashes is not me'ilah,
chunks.st: And the sixth ordinance concerned the red heifer: that deriving benefit from its ashes is not considered misusing consecrated property.

chunks.en: and about bird pairs that became pasul,
chunks.st: And the seventh ordinance was about disqualified pairs of bird-offerings:

words.note: Not good to be brought as a korban.

chunks.en: that new ones come from the money of the community.
chunks.st: It ruled that their replacements should come from public funds.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei disagreed and says:

chunks.en: The one who supplies the bird pairs
chunks.st: The expense does not fall upon the public, but rather upon whoever supplies all the pairs of bird-offerings to the Temple;

chunks.en: supplies the ones that became pasul.
chunks.st: he must also supply, at no additional charge, the replacements for the disqualified birds.

mishnayos.summary: Is spit found in Yerushalayim tahor or tamei? Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei decide by where it was found and whether it was Yom Tov time.

chunks.en: All spit found in Yerushalayim is tahor,
chunks.explain: Most people there were careful to stay tahor.
chunks.st: All the spittle that is found in Jerusalem is ritually pure.
chunks.stMore: Since neither ritually impure people nor gentiles were commonly present in Jerusalem, the Sages decreed an exception to the rule that spittle that is found is ritually impure since it presumably comes from one of those groups.

chunks.en: except for spit in the upper market.
chunks.st: This is the case except for spittle found in the upper marketplace,
chunks.stMore: where gentiles and ritually impure Jews were likely to be present.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: During the rest of the year,
chunks.st: On all the other days of the year,
chunks.stMore: i.e., any day that is not on one of the three pilgrim Festivals, Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot,

chunks.en: spit in the middle of the street is tamei,
chunks.st: spittle that is found in the middle of the street is ritually impure,

chunks.en: and spit on the sides is tahor.
chunks.explain: People who were tamei walked in the middle, and others walked on the sides.
chunks.st: and spittle that is found on the sides of the street is ritually pure. According to Rabbi Yosei,
chunks.stMore: it was common for people who were ritually impure to be present in the streets of Jerusalem. They would be careful to walk in the middle of the street, while the ritually pure who wished to remain so would walk on the sides. Therefore, it is reasonable to presume that spittle found in the middle of the street is from one who is impure, while spittle found on the side of the street is from one who is pure.

words.en: and that is on the sides

chunks.en: But at Yom Tov time,
chunks.st: But during the time of the Festival,
chunks.stMore: when most of the people in Jerusalem were there for the Festival and were ritually pure,

chunks.en: spit in the middle is tahor,
chunks.st: the spittle found in the middle of the street was ritually pure,

chunks.en: and spit on the sides is tamei,
chunks.st: and that found on the sides of the street was ritually impure.

words.en: and that is on the sides

chunks.en: because the few who are tamei move to the sides.
chunks.st: The difference is due to the fact that at the time of the Festival, the ritually impure minority moves to the sides of the streets.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna discusses the ritual purity of items found either in the Temple or in Jerusalem and its environs, in continuation of the previous chapter’s discussion of found money, animals, or meat.

mishnayos.summary: Vessels found on the way down to the mikveh are tamei, and on the way up are tahor, says Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yosei says they are all tahor, except for tools used at graves.

chunks.en: All vessels found in Yerushalayim
chunks.st: All the vessels that are found in Jerusalem

chunks.en: on the way down to the mikveh are tamei.
chunks.st: on the way down into the bathhouse, wherein one purifies vessels in a ritual bath, are ritually impure,

words.note: The mikveh, where vessels are dipped to become tahor.

chunks.en: On the way up, they are tahor,
chunks.st: and those that are found on the way up are ritually pure.

chunks.en: because the way down is not the way up.
chunks.st: The mishna explains: Their descent into the bathhouse is not by the same route as their ascent out of it,
chunks.stMore: and it can be assumed that those found on the way down have not yet been immersed, while those found on the way up have been.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: However, Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: They are all tahor,
chunks.st: They are all ritually pure,

chunks.en: except for the basket, the shovel
chunks.st: except for the basket, and the shovel,

chunks.en: and the pickax that are used for graves.
chunks.st: and the meritza, which are specifically used for graves, to gather up the bones of the dead.
chunks.stMore: These tools must be presumed to be ritually impure, but in general, vessels are presumed to be pure.

mishnayos.summary: Is a knife found right before Pesach tahor, so it can be used for the korban Pesach? It depends on what day it was found and what kind of knife it is.

chunks.he: סַכִּין שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, שׁוֹחֵט בָּהּ מִיָּד.
chunks.en: A knife found on the fourteenth of Nisan, one may shecht with it right away.
chunks.explain: Its owner surely dipped it in a mikveh the day before.
chunks.st: One may slaughter immediately with a knife that was found on the fourteenth of Nisan,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the day the Paschal lamb is slaughtered, and need not be concerned that it is ritually impure. Presumably it was immersed the day before so that it could be used to slaughter the Paschal offering.

chunks.en: On the thirteenth, he dips it in a mikveh again.
chunks.st: If he found it on the thirteenth of Nisan, he immerses it again.
chunks.stMore: Perhaps its owners had not yet immersed it, since they still had time to do so before the evening.

chunks.en: A cleaver,
chunks.st: If one finds a cleaver [kofitz], which is used to slaughter an animal and break its bones,

words.note: A heavy knife for cutting bones.

chunks.he: בֵּין בָּזֶה וּבֵין בָּזֶה שׁוֹנֶה וּמַטְבִּיל.
chunks.en: whether on this day or that day, he dips it again.
chunks.explain: The bones of the korban Pesach may not be broken, so no one used it that day.
chunks.st: whether it was on this day, i.e., the fourteenth, or on that day, i.e., the thirteenth, he immerses it again out of doubt.
chunks.stMore: Since breaking the bones of the Paschal lamb is prohibited, its owners would have no need for it on the fourteenth, and it cannot be presumed that it has already been immersed to make it ritually pure.

chunks.en: If the fourteenth falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: However, if the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: he may shecht with it right away.
chunks.st: he may slaughter with the cleaver immediately.
chunks.stMore: Since immersing a vessel is prohibited on Shabbat, and presumably the owner of the cleaver wants it to be ritually pure on the fifteenth, one can assume that he immersed it already on Friday, the thirteenth of Nisan. It is therefore ritually pure.

chunks.en: If found on the fifteenth, he may shecht with it right away.
chunks.st: If the cleaver was found on the fifteenth of Nisan, i.e., if it was found on the Festival itself, he may slaughter with it immediately.
chunks.stMore: The owners of the cleaver would have immersed it so that they could use it on the fifteenth to cut up the bones of a Festival peace-offering.

chunks.en: If it was found tied to a knife,
chunks.st: If the cleaver was found attached to a knife,

chunks.en: it is like the knife.
chunks.st: it is like a knife,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if it was found on the thirteenth of Nisan it is presumed impure, and if it was found on the fourteenth he may slaughter with it immediately, as it was certainly immersed on the day before.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna continues with another ruling about ritual purity:

mishnayos.summary: If the Paroches became tamei, how and where was it dipped in a mikveh? A new Paroches was spread out where everyone could see how beautiful it was.

chunks.en: A Paroches that became tamei from a smaller kind of tumah
chunks.st: With regard to a curtain that became ritually impure from a secondary source of impurity,
chunks.stMore: since its ritual impurity is by rabbinic law and not Torah law, there is no need to remove it from the Temple.

words.note: The curtain in front of the Kodesh HaKodashim.

chunks.en: is dipped in a mikveh inside
chunks.st: Rather, it is immersed inside the Temple.

chunks.en: and brought back in right away.
chunks.st: And if it were removed to outside the courtyard in order to immerse it, it can be brought back into the courtyard immediately.
chunks.stMore: Since it is ritually impure only by rabbinic law, there is no need to wait until sunset before returning it.

chunks.en: One that became tamei from a stronger kind of tumah
chunks.st: But if it became impure from a primary source of impurity,
chunks.stMore: e.g., it came into contact with the carcass of one of the eight creeping animals that confer impurity by Torah law,

chunks.he: מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתָהּ בַּחוּץ וְשׁוֹטְחִין אוֹתָהּ בַּחֵיל.
chunks.en: is dipped outside and spread out on the Cheil.
chunks.explain: It must wait until nighttime to become tahor.
chunks.st: it is immersed outside the courtyard and is spread out to dry on the rampart. This is the low wall surrounding the Temple courtyard and the buildings within it, which has a lower level of holiness than the courtyard. The reason for this policy is because the sun needs to set on it.
chunks.stMore: Immersion does not confer ritual purity on an item that became impure by Torah law until after the sun has set.

words.note: A low wall around the Azarah.

chunks.en: And if it was new,
chunks.st: And if this curtain were new,

chunks.en: it was spread out on the roof of the bench,
chunks.st: it is spread out to dry on top of the bench [itztabba], a prominent place on the Temple Mount,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאוּ הָעָם אֶת מְלַאכְתָּהּ שֶׁהִיא נָאָה:
chunks.en: so the people could see its beautiful work.
chunks.st: so that the people will see its craftsmanship and perceive its beauty.

mishnayos.summary: The Paroches was very thick and big, made of many threads. Two were made every year, and it was so heavy that three hundred Kohanim dipped it in the mikveh.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says

chunks.en: in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan,
chunks.st: in the name of Rabbi Shimon the son of the deputy High Priest:

chunks.en: The Paroches is a tefach thick,
chunks.st: The curtain has the thickness of a handbreadth,

words.note: About the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and it is woven of seventy-two strands,
chunks.st: and it is woven from seventy-two strands of yarn.

chunks.he: וְעַל כָּל נִימָא וְנִימָא עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חוּטִין.
chunks.en: and each strand has twenty-four threads.
chunks.st: And each and every strand from those seventy-two is made from twenty-four threads. The curtain was made from four materials:
chunks.stMore: Sky-blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and fine linen, and a strand was made up of six threads of each type of material.

chunks.en: It is forty amos long
chunks.st: And with regard to the dimensions of the curtain, its length was forty cubits, as the height of the ceiling of the Sanctuary;

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm.

chunks.en: and twenty amos wide,
chunks.st: and its width was twenty cubits, to match the width of the entrance;

chunks.en: and it cost eight hundred twenty thousand gold coins.
chunks.st: and it was made from eighty-two ten-thousands, i.e., 820,000 golden dinar.

chunks.en: They made two every year,
chunks.st: And they used to make two new curtains every year.

chunks.en: and three hundred Kohanim dip it in a mikveh.
chunks.st: And the curtain was so heavy that they needed three hundred priests to carry it when they would immerse it.

mishnayos.stIntro: The Gemara discusses the aforementioned curtain that separated the Holy of Holies from the Sanctuary.

mishnayos.summary: If very holy korban meat became tamei, it must be burned. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue whether it is burned inside or outside the Azarah.

chunks.en: Meat of the holiest korbanos that became tamei,
chunks.st: With regard to the flesh of offerings of the most sacred order that became impure,

words.note: The holiest kinds of korbanos.

chunks.he: בֵּין בְּאַב הַטֻמְאָה, בֵּין בִּוְלַד הַטֻמְאָה,
chunks.en: whether from a strong kind of tumah or a smaller kind of tumah,
chunks.st: whether it became impure from a primary source of impurity or from a secondary source of impurity,

chunks.en: whether inside or outside,
chunks.st: whether it became impure inside the courtyard or outside, it must be burned.
chunks.stMore: There is a dispute among the tanna’im with regard to where it is burned.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: it is all burned inside,
chunks.st: It all should be burned inside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: except what became tamei outside from a strong tumah.
chunks.st: except for that which became impure from a primary source of ritual impurity outside, as under such circumstances,
chunks.stMore: it is not appropriate to bring it inside the Temple.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: it is all burned outside,
chunks.st: It all should be burned outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: except what became tamei inside from a smaller tumah.
chunks.st: except for that which became ritually impure by a secondary source of impurity inside.
chunks.stMore: In such a case the flesh need not be removed from the courtyard and is burned there.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer says it depends on what kind of tumah the meat got. Rabbi Akiva says it is burned in the same place where it became tamei.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: What became tamei from a strong kind of tumah,
chunks.st: Flesh from offerings of the most sacred order that became ritually impure from a primary source of ritual impurity,

chunks.en: whether inside or outside,
chunks.st: whether it became so inside the courtyard or outside,

chunks.en: is burned outside.
chunks.st: is burned outside.
chunks.stMore: Since its ritual impurity is of the most stringent type, it is not to be brought into the courtyard, or allowed to remain there.

chunks.en: And what became tamei from a smaller kind of tumah,
chunks.st: However, an item that became ritually impure from a secondary source of ritual impurity,

chunks.en: whether inside or outside,
chunks.st: whether it became ritually impure outside or inside,

chunks.en: is burned inside.
chunks.st: is burned inside.
chunks.stMore: Since its ritual impurity is of a lenient type, it can be brought into the courtyard in order to be burned.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: Where it became tamei, there it is burned.
chunks.st: The place of its impurity is where its burning should occur. Therefore,
chunks.stMore: regardless of whether the source is primary or secondary, such flesh is burned wherever it presently is.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells where the parts of different korbanos were put on the ramp before going on the mizbeach. It also teaches which mitzvos apply only when the Beis HaMikdash stands.

chunks.en: The parts of the korban tamid
chunks.st: The limbs of the daily offering
chunks.stMore: were not placed directly on the altar fire. Instead, after cutting up the offering, its limbs

words.note: The korban brought every morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: are put on the lower half of the ramp, on the east side.
chunks.st: were placed first on the ramp of the altar, from the halfway point and below, on the lower sixteen cubits of the ramp, on its western side.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz and Bartenura have a version that says west here, and east for the musaf.

chunks.he: וְשֶׁל מוּסָפִין נִתָּנִין מֵחֲצִי כֶּבֶשׁ וּלְמַטָה בַּמַּעֲרָב,
chunks.en: And those of the musaf korbanos are put on the lower half of the ramp, on the west side.
chunks.st: Limbs of the additional offerings of the Shabbat and Festivals were placed on the ramp from the halfway point and below on its eastern side.

chunks.en: And those of Rosh Chodesh are put
chunks.st: Additional New Moon offerings were placed

chunks.en: below the edge of the mizbeach.
chunks.st: on top of the upper part of the edge [karkov] of the altar.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz and Bartenura say they were put on the upper part, on the edge.

chunks.he: הַשְּׁקָלִים וְהַבִּכּוּרִים אֵין נוֹהֲגִין אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: Shekalim and bikkurim are only kept while the Beis HaMikdash stands,
chunks.st: Another law: The obligation to give half-shekels each year and to offer the first fruits is practiced only in the presence of the Temple,as fulfillment of these mitzvot is only possible then.

words.note: The first fruits brought to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: אֲבָל מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן וּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וְהַבְּכוֹרוֹת
chunks.en: but maaser of grain, maaser of animals, and firstborn animals
chunks.st: But the mitzvot of produce tithes and grain tithes and of animal tithes and of the sanctified firstborn animals

chunks.en: apply both when the Beis HaMikdash stands
chunks.st: are practiced whether one is in the presence of the Temple,

chunks.en: and when it does not.
chunks.st: or one is not in the presence of the Temple.
chunks.stMore: Although animal tithes and firstborn cannot be sacrificed without a Temple, once they develop a blemish, they may be eaten by their owners.

chunks.en: If someone makes shekalim or bikkurim hekdesh,
chunks.st: If, in the present time when there is no Temple, one consecrates shekels for the mitzva of the half-shekel or fruits for the mitzva of first fruits,

chunks.en: they are holy.
chunks.explain: Even when there is no Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: they are consecrated, and it is prohibited to derive benefit from them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: If someone says "These bikkurim are holy,"
chunks.st: One who declared first fruits to be consecrated,

chunks.en: they are not holy.
chunks.st: in the present time, does not give them that status and they are not consecrated.
